/**
 * CANopen configuration, used with @ref CO_new()
 *
 * This structure is used only, if @ref CO_MULTIPLE_OD is enabled. Otherwise parameters are retrieved from default
 * "OD.h" file.
 */
typedef struct {
    uint8_t CNT_NMT;         /**< Number of NMT objects, 0 or 1: NMT slave (CANrx) + Heartbeat producer (CANtx) +
                                optional NMT master (CANtx), configurable by @ref CO_CONFIG_NMT. Start indexes inside
                                CANrx and CANtx are always 0. There must be one NMT object in the device. */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1017; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_NMT_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_HB_CONS;     /**< Number of Heartbeat consumer objects, 0 or 1 */
    uint8_t CNT_ARR_1016; /**< Number of internal consumers (CANrx), used inside Heartbeat consumer object, 1 to 127. */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1016; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_HBconsumer_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H100C; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_nodeGuardingSlave_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H100D; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_nodeGuardingSlave_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_EM; /**< Number of Emergency objects, 0 or 1: optional producer (CANtx) + optional consumer (CANrx),
                       configurable by @ref CO_CONFIG_EM. There must be one Emergency object in the device. */
    const OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1001; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_EM_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1014;       /**< OD entry for @ref CO_EM_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1015;       /**< OD entry for @ref CO_EM_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_ARR_1003;    /**< Size of the fifo buffer, which is used for intermediate storage of emergency messages.
                                Fifo is used by emergency producer and by error history (OD object 0x1003). Size is usually
                                equal to size of array in OD object 0x1003. If later is not used, CNT_ARR_1003 must also be
                                set to value greater than 0, or emergency producer will not work. */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1003; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_EM_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_SDO_SRV;     /**< Number of SDO server objects, from 0 to 128 (CANrx + CANtx). There must be at least
                                one SDO server object in the device. */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1200; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SDOserver_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_SDO_CLI;     /**< Number of SDO client objects, from 0 to 128 (CANrx + CANtx). */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1280; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SDOclient_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_TIME;        /**< Number of TIME objects, 0 or 1: consumer (CANrx) + optional producer (CANtx),
                                configurable by @ref CO_CONFIG_TIME. */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1012; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_TIME_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_SYNC;        /**< Number of SYNC objects, 0 or 1:  consumer (CANrx) + optional producer (CANtx),
                                configurable by @ref CO_CONFIG_SYNC. */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1005; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SYNC_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1006; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SYNC_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1007; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SYNC_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1019; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SYNC_init() */
    uint16_t CNT_RPDO;       /**< Number of RPDO objects, from 0 to 512 consumers (CANrx) */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1400; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_RPDO_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1600; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_RPDO_init() */
    uint16_t CNT_TPDO;       /**< Number of TPDO objects, from 0 to 512 producers (CANtx) */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1800; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_TPDO_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1A00; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_TPDO_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_LEDS;        /**< Number of LEDs objects, 0 or 1. */
    uint8_t CNT_GFC;         /**< Number of GFC objects, 0 or 1 (CANrx + CANtx). */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1300; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_GFC_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_SRDO;        /**< Number of SRDO objects, from 0 to 64 (2*CANrx + 2*CANtx). */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1301; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SRDO_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H1381; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SRDO_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H13FE; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SRDO_init() */
    OD_entry_t* ENTRY_H13FF; /**< OD entry for @ref CO_SRDO_init() */
    uint8_t CNT_LSS_SLV;     /**< Number of LSSslave objects, 0 or 1 (CANrx + CANtx). */
    uint8_t CNT_LSS_MST;     /**< Number of LSSmaster objects, 0 or 1 (CANrx + CANtx). */
    uint8_t CNT_GTWA;        /**< Number of gateway ascii objects, 0 or 1. */
    uint16_t CNT_TRACE;      /**< Number of trace objects, 0 or more. */
} CO_config_t;

typedef struct {
    void* CANptr;                    /**< From CO_CANmodule_init() */
    CO_CANrx_t* rxArray;             /**< From CO_CANmodule_init() */
    uint16_t rxSize;                 /**< From CO_CANmodule_init() */
    CO_CANtx_t* txArray;             /**< From CO_CANmodule_init() */
    uint16_t txSize;                 /**< From CO_CANmodule_init() */
    uint16_t CANerrorStatus;         /**< CAN error status bitfield, see @ref CO_CAN_ERR_status_t */
    volatile bool_t CANnormal;       /**< CAN module is in normal mode */
    volatile bool_t useCANrxFilters; /**< Value different than zero indicates, that CAN module hardware filters are used
                                        for CAN reception. If there is not enough hardware filters, they won't be used.
                                        In this case will be *all* received CAN messages processed by software. */
    volatile bool_t bufferInhibitFlag; /**< If flag is true, then message in transmit buffer is synchronous PDO message,
                                          which will be aborted, if CO_clearPendingSyncPDOs() function will be called by
                                          application. This may be necessary if Synchronous window time was expired. */
    volatile bool_t
        firstCANtxMessage; /**< Equal to 1, when the first transmitted message (bootup message) is in CAN TX buffers */
    volatile uint16_t
        CANtxCount;  /**< Number of messages in transmit buffer, which are waiting to be copied to the CAN module */
    uint32_t errOld; /**< Previous state of CAN errors */
} CO_CANmodule_t;

typedef struct {
    /** Object Dictionary stream object, passed to read or write */
    OD_stream_t stream;
    /**
     * Function pointer for reading value from specified variable from Object Dictionary. If OD variable is larger than
     * buf, then this function must be called several times. After completed successful read function returns 'ODR_OK'.
     * If read is partial, it returns 'ODR_PARTIAL'. In case of errors function returns code similar to SDO abort code.
     *
     * Read can be restarted with @ref OD_rwRestart() function.
     *
     * At the moment, when Object Dictionary is initialized, every variable has assigned the same "read" function. This
     * default function simply copies data from Object Dictionary variable. Application can bind its own "read" function
     * for specific object. In that case application is able to calculate data for reading from own internal state at
     * the moment of "read" function call. Own "read" function on OD object can be initialized with @ref
     * OD_extension_init() function.
     *
     * "read" function must always copy all own data to buf, except if "buf" is not large enough. ("*returnCode" must
     * not return 'ODR_PARTIAL', if there is still space in "buf".)
     *
     * @warning Do not use @ref CO_LOCK_OD() and @ref CO_UNLOCK_OD() macros inside the read() function. See also @ref
     * CO_critical_sections.
     *
     * @param stream Object Dictionary stream object.
     * @param buf Pointer to external buffer, where to data will be copied.
     * @param count Size of the external buffer in bytes.
     * @param [out] countRead If return value is "ODR_OK" or "ODR_PARTIAL", then number of bytes successfully read must
     * be returned here.
     *
     * @return Value from @ref ODR_t, "ODR_OK" in case of success.
     */
    ODR_t (*read)(OD_stream_t* stream, void* buf, OD_size_t count, OD_size_t* countRead);
    /**
     * Function pointer for writing value into specified variable inside Object Dictionary. If OD variable is larger
     * than buf, then this function must be called several times. After completed successful write function returns
     * 'ODR_OK'. If write is partial, it returns 'ODR_PARTIAL'. In case of errors function returns code similar to SDO
     * abort code.
     *
     * Write can be restarted with @ref OD_rwRestart() function.
     *
     * At the moment, when Object Dictionary is initialized, every variable has assigned the same "write" function,
     * which simply copies data to Object Dictionary variable. Application can bind its own "write" function, similar as
     * it can bind "read" function.
     *
     * "write" function must always copy all available data from buf. If OD variable expect more data, then
     * "*returnCode" must return 'ODR_PARTIAL'.
     *
     * @warning Do not use @ref CO_LOCK_OD() and @ref CO_UNLOCK_OD() macros inside the write() function. See also @ref
     * CO_critical_sections.
     *
     * @param stream Object Dictionary stream object.
     * @param buf Pointer to external buffer, from where data will be copied.
     * @param count Size of the external buffer in bytes.
     * @param [out] countWritten If return value is "ODR_OK" or "ODR_PARTIAL", then number of bytes successfully written
     * must be returned here.
     *
     * @return Value from @ref ODR_t, "ODR_OK" in case of success.
     */
    ODR_t (*write)(OD_stream_t* stream, const void* buf, OD_size_t count, OD_size_t* countWritten);
} OD_IO_t;

functions.name: CO_new
functions.signature: CO_t* CO_new(CO_config_t* config, uint32_t* heapMemoryUsed);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a CANopenNode stack instance (CO_t). Uses global statics if CO_USE_GLOBALS is defined; otherwise allocates from the heap. The optional heapMemoryUsed out-parameter reports total heap consumed. If CO_MULTIPLE_OD is enabled, the provided config describes how many/which objects to create and must remain valid for the lifetime of the CO_t. Returns NULL on allocation/configuration failure.
requirements: If CO_MULTIPLE_OD is defined: config must be a valid CO_config_t and must remain allocated for the lifetime of the CO_t.
If CO_MULTIPLE_OD is not defined: pass config == NULL; parameters are taken from OD.h.
Caller must check the return value for NULL before use.
If heap is used, the environment must provide sufficient heap (may require linker heap size configuration on some MCUs).
heapMemoryUsed may be NULL; if non-NULL it is written with the number of bytes used.

functions.name: CO_delete
functions.signature: void CO_delete(CO_t* co);
functions.description: Deletes a CANopenNode instance and frees associated resources. Intended to be called at program exit to release memory allocated by CO_new.
requirements: co must be a valid pointer previously returned by CO_new.
Must not be called multiple times on the same instance (no double free).
Must not be called concurrently with other CO_* processing on the same instance.

functions.name: CO_isLSSslaveEnabled
functions.signature: bool_t CO_isLSSslaveEnabled(CO_t* co);
functions.description: Checks whether the LSS (Layer Setting Services) slave functionality is enabled for the given CANopen instance. Returns true if enabled, false otherwise.
requirements: co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.

functions.name: CO_CANinit
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_CANinit(CO_t* co, void* CANptr, uint16_t bitRate);
functions.description: Initializes the CAN driver/module used by the CANopen stack. Must be invoked during the communication reset section. CANptr is a user-defined handle passed down to CO_CANmodule_init().
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section (before higher-level CANopen object initialization that depends on CAN).
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
CANptr must be a valid pointer to the user-defined CAN base structure expected by CO_CANmodule_init().
bitRate must be a valid CAN bit rate supported by the underlying driver.
Caller must check the returned CO_ReturnError_t; CO_ERROR_NO indicates success.

functions.name: CO_LSSinit
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_LSSinit(CO_t* co, CO_LSS_address_t* lssAddress, uint8_t* pendingNodeID, uint16_t* pendingBitRate);
functions.description: Initializes the CANopen LSS (Layer Setting Services) slave for node-ID/bit-rate configuration over CAN. Must be called before CO_CANopenInit. The lssAddress is typically taken from OD object 0x1018. pendingNodeID is an in/out parameter holding the pending node-ID (0xFF means unconfigured). pendingBitRate is an in/out parameter holding the pending CAN bit rate. Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success. Available only when LSS slave support is enabled at compile time.
requirements: Must be called before CO_CANopenInit().
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
lssAddress must point to a valid CO_LSS_address_t, typically initialized from OD 0x1018.
pendingNodeID must be non-NULL; input of 0xFF indicates unconfigured; it may be updated by the function.
pendingBitRate must be non-NULL; it may be updated by the function.
Caller must check the returned CO_ReturnError_t; CO_ERROR_NO indicates success.
This function is available only if ((CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_SLAVE) != 0).

functions.name: CO_CANopenInit
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_CANopenInit(CO_t* co, CO_NMT_t* NMT, CO_EM_t* em, OD_t* od, OD_entry_t* OD_statusBits, uint16_t NMTcontrol, uint16_t firstHBTime_ms, uint16_t SDOserverTimeoutTime_ms, uint16_t SDOclientTimeoutTime_ms, bool_t SDOclientBlockTransfer, uint8_t nodeId, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initializes the CANopenNode stack, except PDO objects. Must be called during the communication reset section. Wires up core services (NMT, emergency, SDO server/client, SYNC/TIME/etc.) using parameters and the object dictionary. If nodeId is 0xFF (unconfigured), some objects will not be initialized/processed. errInfo provides additional detail on errors and may also be set in noncritical situations.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section (before starting processing and before PDO init).
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
od must be a valid pointer to the CANopen Object Dictionary (OD_t).
em may be NULL to use co->em; if em is NULL and the configured number of Emergency objects (CNT_EM) is 0, the function returns an error.
If the configured number of NMT objects (CNT_NMT) is 0, NMT must be a valid pointer; if CNT_NMT is 1, NMT is ignored and may be NULL.
OD_statusBits may be NULL; if non-NULL it is passed to CO_EM_init().
NMTcontrol, firstHBTime_ms, SDOserverTimeoutTime_ms, SDOclientTimeoutTime_ms, and SDOclientBlockTransfer are forwarded to respective init functions and must be valid values for those subsystems.
nodeId must be 1..127 or 0xFF (unconfigured).
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL it may be written with additional error information even when CO_ERROR_NO is returned.
Caller must check the returned CO_ReturnError_t; CO_ERROR_NO indicates success.

functions.name: CO_CANopenInitPDO
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_CANopenInitPDO(CO_t* co, CO_EM_t* em, OD_t* od, uint8_t nodeId, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initializes PDO (Process Data Object) modules. Must be called at the end of the communication reset section after all CANopen and application initialization so that OD variables are correctly mapped into PDOs. If nodeId is 0xFF (unconfigured), PDOs will not be initialized nor processed.
requirements: Must be called after CO_CANopenInit() and after application has completed initialization/configuration of OD mappings.
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
em must be a valid Emergency object used for PDO error reporting.
od must be a valid pointer to the CANopen Object Dictionary (OD_t).
nodeId must be 1..127 or 0xFF (unconfigured).
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL it may be written with additional error information.
Caller must check the returned CO_ReturnError_t; CO_ERROR_NO indicates success.

functions.name: CO_CANopenInitSRDO
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_CANopenInitSRDO(CO_t* co, CO_EM_t* em, OD_t* od, uint8_t nodeId, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initializes SRDO (Safety Related Data Object) and GFC components when enabled. Must be called at the end of the communication reset section after all CANopen and application initialization so OD variables are correctly mapped. If the node is unconfigured (nodeId 0xFF), the safety-related objects will not be initialized nor processed. Available only when GFC and/or SRDO are enabled at compile time.
requirements: Must be called after CO_CANopenInit() and after application/OD setup is complete to ensure correct mappings.
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
em must be a valid Emergency object used for error reporting in SRDO/GFC.
od must be a valid pointer to the CANopen Object Dictionary (OD_t).
nodeId must be 1..127 or 0xFF (unconfigured).
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL it may be written with additional error information.
Caller must check the returned CO_ReturnError_t; CO_ERROR_NO indicates success.
This function is available only if ((CO_CONFIG_GFC & CO_CONFIG_GFC_ENABLE) != 0) or ((CO_CONFIG_SRDO & CO_CONFIG_SRDO_ENABLE) != 0).

functions.name: CO_process
functions.signature: CO_NMT_reset_cmd_t CO_process(CO_t* co, bool_t enableGateway, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Main cyclic processing for asynchronous CANopen objects (e.g., NMT heartbeat, SDO timeouts, HB consumer, etc.). Should be called periodically. If enableGateway is true, the ASCII gateway (if compiled in) is enabled. timeDifference_us is the elapsed time since the previous call. timerNext_us, if provided, is used to inform the OS of the maximum delay before the next call; caller must preset it to the maximum allowed interval and the function will reduce it as needed.
requirements: Must be called cyclically throughout runtime.
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
enableGateway controls whether the gateway to external world is enabled; set appropriately for the application.
timeDifference_us must be the time since the last CO_process() call in microseconds.
If timerNext_us is non-NULL, the caller must initialize *timerNext_us to the maximum allowed interval before calling; on return it will be reduced to the required next wake-up time.
timerNext_us may be NULL to ignore timing hints.
Return value must be checked for node/communication reset requests per CO_NMT_process().
Should be used together with callbacks configured via CO_***_initCallbackPre(); those callbacks should also trigger CO_process() calls.

functions.name: CO_process_SYNC
functions.signature: bool_t CO_process_SYNC(CO_t* co, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Cyclic processing of SYNC producer/consumer. For time-critical applications it may be called from a real-time thread at a constant interval (typically 1 ms). Returns true if a SYNC was just received or transmitted.
requirements: Must be called cyclically; for time-critical paths, call from a real-time context with a constant interval (≈1 ms typical).
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
timeDifference_us must be the time since the last CO_process_SYNC() call in microseconds.
If timerNext_us is non-NULL, initialize it to the maximum allowed interval before call; on return it will be reduced to the required next wake-up time.
timerNext_us may be NULL to ignore timing hints.
This function is available only if ((CO_CONFIG_SYNC & CO_CONFIG_SYNC_ENABLE) != 0).

functions.name: CO_process_RPDO
functions.signature: void CO_process_RPDO(CO_t* co, bool_t syncWas, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Cyclic processing of receive PDOs. For time-critical applications it may be called from a real-time thread with a constant interval (typically 1 ms). syncWas should reflect whether a SYNC occurred in the current cycle (e.g., result from CO_process_SYNC).
requirements: Must be called cyclically; for time-critical paths, call from a real-time context with a constant interval (≈1 ms typical).
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
syncWas must indicate whether a SYNC was just received or transmitted in this cycle.
timeDifference_us must be the time since the last CO_process_RPDO() call in microseconds.
If timerNext_us is non-NULL, initialize it to the maximum allowed interval before call; on return it will be reduced to the required next wake-up time.
timerNext_us may be NULL to ignore timing hints.
This function is available only if ((CO_CONFIG_PDO & CO_CONFIG_RPDO_ENABLE) != 0).

functions.name: CO_process_TPDO
functions.signature: void CO_process_TPDO(CO_t* co, bool_t syncWas, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Cyclic processing of transmit PDOs. For time-critical applications it may be called from a real-time thread with a constant interval (typically 1 ms). syncWas should reflect whether a SYNC occurred in the current cycle (e.g., result from CO_process_SYNC).
requirements: Must be called cyclically; for time-critical paths, call from a real-time context with a constant interval (≈1 ms typical).
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
syncWas must indicate whether a SYNC was just received or transmitted in this cycle.
timeDifference_us must be the time since the last CO_process_TPDO() call in microseconds.
If timerNext_us is non-NULL, initialize it to the maximum allowed interval before call; on return it will be reduced to the required next wake-up time.
timerNext_us may be NULL to ignore timing hints.
This function is available only if ((CO_CONFIG_PDO & CO_CONFIG_TPDO_ENABLE) != 0).

functions.name: CO_process_SRDO
functions.signature: CO_SRDO_state_t CO_process_SRDO(CO_t* co, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Cyclic processing of Safety Related Data Objects (and associated guard). For time-critical applications it may be called from a real-time thread with a constant interval (typically 1 ms). Returns the lowest state across SRDO objects.
requirements: Must be called cyclically; for time-critical paths, call from a real-time context with a constant interval (≈1 ms typical).
co must be a valid pointer to a CO_t.
timeDifference_us must be the time since the last CO_process_SRDO() call in microseconds.
If timerNext_us is non-NULL, initialize it to the maximum allowed interval before call; on return it will be reduced to the required next wake-up time.
timerNext_us may be NULL to ignore timing hints.
This function is available only if ((CO_CONFIG_SRDO & CO_CONFIG_SRDO_ENABLE) != 0).

functions.name: CANrx_callback
functions.signature: void CANrx_callback(void* object, void* rxMsg);
functions.description: Pre-processing callback invoked by the fast CAN receive thread when a message matches a configured receive buffer. Each CANopen object registers its own callback via CO_CANrxBufferInit. Reads fields from rxMsg and stores data into the object, then typically signals new data for deferred processing.
requirements: object must be the same pointer supplied when configuring the receive buffer with CO_CANrxBufferInit.
rxMsg must point to the target-specific received CAN message structure.
Callback must be fast and non-blocking, suitable for IRQ/real-time context.
If it sets any new_message flags, it should ensure proper memory barriers as required by the platform.

functions.name: CO_CANrxMsg_readIdent
functions.signature: static inline uint16_t CO_CANrxMsg_readIdent(void* rxMsg);
functions.description: Target-specific helper to read the 11-bit standard CAN identifier (and possibly RTR bit alignment) from a received message object. Intended to be used inside CANrx_callback.
requirements: rxMsg must point to a valid target-specific CAN receive message.
Returns the 11-bit standard identifier; interpretation of any additional bits (e.g., RTR at bit 11) is target-specific.
Must be provided by the target (typically as an inline/macro in CO_driver_target.h); the body here is a placeholder.

functions.name: CO_CANrxMsg_readDLC
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t CO_CANrxMsg_readDLC(void* rxMsg);
functions.description: Target-specific helper to read the Data Length Code (0..8) from a received CAN message. Intended for use in CANrx_callback.
requirements: rxMsg must point to a valid target-specific CAN receive message.
Return value is the data length in bytes and must be in the range 0..8.
Must be provided by the target implementation; the body here is a placeholder.

functions.name: CO_CANrxMsg_readData
functions.signature: static inline const uint8_t* CO_CANrxMsg_readData(void* rxMsg);
functions.description: Target-specific helper to obtain a pointer to the payload bytes of a received CAN message. Intended for use in CANrx_callback.
requirements: rxMsg must point to a valid target-specific CAN receive message.
Returned pointer must reference at least DLC bytes as reported by CO_CANrxMsg_readDLC.
Must be provided by the target implementation; the body here is a placeholder.

functions.name: CO_CANsetConfigurationMode
functions.signature: void CO_CANsetConfigurationMode(void* CANptr);
functions.description: Puts the CAN controller into configuration (stopped) mode and waits until the mode is entered. Used before initializing or reconfiguring the CAN module.
requirements: CANptr must be a valid pointer to the target CAN device/controller.
Must be called before CO_CANmodule_init per the initialization sequence.

functions.name: CO_CANsetNormalMode
functions.signature: void CO_CANsetNormalMode(CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule);
functions.description: Requests normal/operational mode for the CAN controller and waits until active. Typically called after successful initialization to start communication.
requirements: CANmodule must be a valid, initialized CO_CANmodule_t instance.
The underlying CAN controller must support switching to normal mode.

functions.name: CO_CANmodule_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_CANmodule_init(CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule, void* CANptr, CO_CANrx_t rxArray[], uint16_t rxSize, CO_CANtx_t txArray[], uint16_t txSize, uint16_t CANbitRate);
functions.description: Initializes the CAN module abstraction and binds it to the target CAN controller, receive buffer array, and transmit buffer array. Must be called during communication reset while the controller is in configuration mode. Sets bitrate and prepares RX/TX structures.
requirements: CAN controller must already be in configuration mode before calling.
CANmodule must be a valid pointer; its fields will be initialized by this call.
rxArray must point to an array of CO_CANrx_t with length rxSize; rxSize must equal the number of receive objects to configure.
txArray must point to an array of CO_CANtx_t with length txSize; txSize must equal the number of transmit objects to configure.
CANbitRate accepted values (kbps): 10, 20, 50, 125, 250, 500, 800, 1000; illegal values default internally to 125 kbps.
Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success or CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid arguments.

functions.name: CO_CANmodule_disable
functions.signature: void CO_CANmodule_disable(CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule);
functions.description: Shuts down the CAN module abstraction and switches off CAN-related processing. Intended to be called at program exit or during deinitialization.
requirements: CANmodule must be a valid CO_CANmodule_t pointer that was previously initialized.

functions.name: CO_CANrxBufferInit
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_CANrxBufferInit(CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule, uint16_t index, uint16_t ident, uint16_t mask, bool_t rtr, void* object, void (*CANrx_callback)(void* object, void* message));
functions.description: Configures a receive buffer entry in the CAN module with a CAN identifier/mask and registers a fast callback and object pointer to handle matching frames. Must be called for each rxArray entry.
requirements: CANmodule must be a valid, initialized module with rxArray and rxSize set.
index must be within [0, rxSize).
ident must be an 11-bit standard ID (0..0x7FF). If multiple entries share the same ident, the lowest index has precedence; later duplicates will be ignored.
mask is an 11-bit mask applied as: (((rcvMsgId ^ ident) & mask) == 0). Commonly 0x7FF.
rtr true enables acceptance of Remote Transmission Request frames for this entry.
object is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; may be NULL if the callback expects it.
CANrx_callback must be a valid function pointer and must be fast/non-blocking (IRQ/real-time safe).
May return CO_ERROR_NO, CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT, or CO_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (e.g., insufficient hardware filters).

functions.name: CO_CANtxBufferInit
functions.signature: CO_CANtx_t* CO_CANtxBufferInit(CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule, uint16_t index, uint16_t ident, bool_t rtr, uint8_t noOfBytes, bool_t syncFlag);
functions.description: Configures a transmit buffer entry with CAN identifier, RTR flag, DLC, and synchronous flag. Returns a pointer to the buffer so the caller can fill the data before transmission via CO_CANsend.
requirements: CANmodule must be a valid, initialized module with txArray and txSize set.
index must be within [0, txSize).
ident must be an 11-bit standard ID (0..0x7FF).
rtr true configures transmission of RTR frames.
noOfBytes must be in range 0..8 (DLC).
syncFlag true marks the buffer for synchronous TPDO handling (must only transmit within the SYNC window).
Returns NULL (0) on wrong/invalid arguments; otherwise returns pointer to CO_CANtx_t entry whose data[8] must be filled before sending.

functions.name: CO_CANsend
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_CANsend(CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule, CO_CANtx_t* buffer);
functions.description: Attempts to send a CAN frame using a previously configured transmit buffer. If a hardware TX mailbox is free, the frame is put on the bus immediately; otherwise the buffer is queued and sent by the TX interrupt when possible. Synchronous TPDOs may be deferred or rejected outside the SYNC window.
requirements: CANmodule must be valid and in normal/operational mode.
buffer must be a pointer returned by CO_CANtxBufferInit for this CANmodule, and its data[0..DLC-1] must be populated before calling.
Caller should be prepared to handle return codes: CO_ERROR_NO, CO_ERROR_TX_OVERFLOW (buffer full), or CO_ERROR_TX_PDO_WINDOW (sync TPDO outside window).
Until the message is copied to the CAN module (i.e., while bufferFull is true), the contents of the buffer must not be modified.

functions.name: CO_CANclearPendingSyncPDOs
functions.signature: void CO_CANclearPendingSyncPDOs(CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule);
functions.description: Aborts any pending synchronous TPDOs that are queued in CAN TX buffers when the system exits the SYNC window. Called by the stack when SYNC time ends to enforce CiA 301 timing rules.
requirements: CANmodule must be a valid module instance.
Should be called at the moment the system transitions out of the SYNC window.

functions.name: CO_CANmodule_process
functions.signature: void CO_CANmodule_process(CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule);
functions.description: Periodic processing hook for the CAN module to evaluate and update CAN error status flags (warning, passive, overflow, bus-off) in CANerrorStatus according to CO_CAN_ERR_status_t.
requirements: CANmodule must be valid.
Must be called cyclically in the main loop or a periodic task to maintain error status.

functions.name: CO_getUint8

functions.description: Reads a uint8_t value from a memory buffer using memmove for safe, alignment-agnostic access.
requirements: buf must point to at least sizeof(uint8_t) readable bytes.

functions.name: CO_getUint16

functions.description: Reads a uint16_t value from a memory buffer using memmove for safe, alignment-agnostic access. Endianness follows target architecture expectations for stored data.
requirements: buf must point to at least sizeof(uint16_t) readable bytes.

requirements: buf must point to at least sizeof(uint8_t) writable bytes.

functions.name: CO_setUint16

functions.name: OD_readOriginal
functions.signature: ODR_t OD_readOriginal(OD_stream_t* stream, void* buf, OD_size_t count, OD_size_t* countRead);
functions.description: Reads data for a sub-object directly from the original Object Dictionary (OD) memory location. Intended to be used by custom IO extensions or as the default read function. Supports partial reads when the OD variable is larger than the provided buffer; may require multiple calls until ODR_OK is returned.
requirements: stream must refer to a valid OD_stream_t obtained from OD_getSub (original or extended).
buf must point to a writable buffer of at least count bytes.
countRead must be non-NULL; on ODR_OK or ODR_PARTIAL it receives the number of bytes read.
Use OD_rwRestart to restart a read sequence if needed.
The function must not be called with NULL stream or buf.

functions.name: OD_writeOriginal

functions.description: Writes data for a sub-object directly to the original Object Dictionary (OD) memory location. Intended to be used by custom IO extensions or as the default write function. Supports partial writes when the OD variable expects more data; may require multiple calls until ODR_OK is returned.
requirements: stream must refer to a valid OD_stream_t obtained from OD_getSub (original or extended).
buf must point to a readable buffer of at least count bytes.
countWritten must be non-NULL; on ODR_OK or ODR_PARTIAL it receives the number of bytes written.
Use OD_rwRestart to restart a write sequence if needed.
The function must not be called with NULL stream or buf.

functions.name: OD_getSub

requirements: entry must point to a valid OD_entry_t.
io must be non-NULL; it is populated on success.
subIndex must exist within the entry; otherwise an ODR_* error is returned.

functions.name: OD_mappable

functions.name: OD_rwRestart
functions.signature: static inline void OD_rwRestart(OD_stream_t* stream);
functions.description: Restarts a read or write operation by resetting the stream's dataOffset to 0. Useful when repeating a transfer sequence.
requirements: stream may be NULL; if non-NULL, dataOffset is set to 0.

functions.name: OD_requestTPDO

requirements: OD_FLAGS_PDO_SIZE must be > 0 at compile time for effect.
entry must be non-NULL and have a non-NULL entry->extension.
subIndex must be less than OD_FLAGS_PDO_SIZE * 8.
The OD variable must be mapped to an event-driven TPDO (transmission type 0, 254, or 255) for a transmission to occur.

functions.name: OD_TPDOtransmitted
functions.signature: static inline bool_t OD_TPDOtransmitted(OD_entry_t* entry, uint8_t subIndex);
functions.description: Checks whether an event-driven TPDO mapped to the given OD variable has been transmitted since the last OD_requestTPDO call. Returns true also if no request was made but a TPDO was transmitted by another event.
requirements: OD_FLAGS_PDO_SIZE must be > 0 at compile time for effect.
entry must be non-NULL and have a non-NULL entry->extension.

functions.name: CO_NMT_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_NMT_init(CO_NMT_t* NMT, OD_entry_t* OD_1017_ProducerHbTime, CO_EM_t* em, uint8_t nodeId, uint16_t NMTcontrol, uint16_t firstHBTime_ms, CO_CANmodule_t* NMT_CANdevRx, uint16_t NMT_rxIdx, uint16_t CANidRxNMT, CO_CANmodule_t* HB_CANdevTx, uint16_t HB_txIdx, uint16_t CANidTxHB, uint32_t* errInfo)
functions.description: Initialize the NMT consumer and Heartbeat producer object for a node. Intended to be called during the communication reset phase to bind OD 0x1017 (Producer Heartbeat Time), emergency, node-ID, control flags, and CAN RX/TX resources. On success, the NMT stack is ready for cyclic processing via CO_NMT_process.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section (explicit).
OD_1017_ProducerHbTime (OD 0x1017, Producer heartbeat time) entry is required; an IO extension is optional for runtime configuration (explicit).
firstHBTime_ms is required; if greater than Producer Heartbeat time, the Producer Heartbeat time will be used instead (explicit).
errInfo is an optional output and may be NULL (explicit).
NMT must point to a valid CO_NMT_t instance (inferred from parameter usage).
em must point to a valid CO_EM_t instance (inferred).
NMT_CANdevRx must be a valid, initialized CAN device; NMT_rxIdx must be a valid receive buffer index for that device; CANidRxNMT must be the CAN identifier used for NMT receive (inferred).
HB_CANdevTx must be a valid, initialized CAN device; HB_txIdx must be a valid transmit buffer index for that device; CANidTxHB must be the CAN identifier used for Heartbeat transmission (inferred).
nodeId should match the device’s configured Node-ID (inferred).
NMTcontrol controls behavior per CO_NMT_control_t flags; choose bits according to desired startup and error behavior (inferred).

functions.name: CO_NMT_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_NMT_initCallbackPre(CO_NMT_t* NMT, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(void* object))
functions.description: Register an optional callback invoked immediately after an NMT message is received (preprocessed). Use this to promptly trigger CO_NMT_process or wake processing tasks upon NMT reception.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_NMT has CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE set (explicit via header guards).
NMT must reference an initialized CO_NMT_t (inferred).
object is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; it may be NULL (explicit).
pFunctSignal may be NULL; if NULL the callback is not called (explicit).
The callback should be lightweight and should promptly trigger processing of CO_NMT_process, as intended by design notes (explicit).

functions.name: CO_NMT_initCallbackChanged
functions.signature: void CO_NMT_initCallbackChanged(CO_NMT_t* NMT, void (*pFunctNMT)(CO_NMT_internalState_t state))
functions.description: Register an optional callback invoked after the NMT state changes. The first invocation occurs immediately upon registration to deliver the current state. Useful to wake tasks that handle NMT events.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_NMT has CO_CONFIG_NMT_CALLBACK_CHANGE set (explicit via header guards).
NMT must reference an initialized CO_NMT_t (inferred).
pFunctNMT may be NULL; if NULL the callback is not called (explicit).
Callback will also be called immediately once to report the current NMT state (explicit).

functions.name: CO_NMT_process
functions.signature: CO_NMT_reset_cmd_t CO_NMT_process(CO_NMT_t* NMT, CO_NMT_internalState_t* NMTstate, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us)
functions.description: Cyclic processing of NMT consumer and Heartbeat producer. Handles received NMT, applies internal commands, updates/produces heartbeat, and manages state transitions. Returns a reset command directive for the application if a reset is requested.
requirements: Must be called cyclically (explicit).
timeDifference_us must be the elapsed time since the previous call, in microseconds (explicit).
If NMTstate is not NULL, the current NMT internal state will be written to it (explicit).
timerNext_us is an output providing the next suggested call time for scheduling (explicit).
NMT must be initialized via CO_NMT_init before use (inferred).
Application must act on the returned CO_NMT_reset_cmd_t to perform required resets (communication, app, quit) as indicated (explicit).
