functions.description: Query the current NMT internal state of a node. If NMT is NULL, returns CO_NMT_INITIALIZING.
requirements: If NMT is NULL, the function returns CO_NMT_INITIALIZING by design (explicit).
For a meaningful state, pass a valid, initialized CO_NMT_t (inferred).

functions.name: CO_NMT_sendInternalCommand
functions.signature: static inline void CO_NMT_sendInternalCommand(CO_NMT_t* NMT, CO_NMT_command_t command)
functions.description: Queue an internal NMT command to be applied to the local node without transmitting an NMT CAN message. The command is validated and processed within CO_NMT_process.
requirements: NMT must not be NULL for the command to take effect (explicit via code path).
CO_NMT_process must be running/called subsequently to process the queued command (explicit).
Command must be a valid CO_NMT_command_t value (inferred).

functions.name: CO_NMT_sendCommand
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_NMT_sendCommand(CO_NMT_t* NMT, CO_NMT_command_t command, uint8_t nodeID)
functions.description: Transmit an NMT master command over CAN to control remote nodes’ NMT states. Typically used only by an NMT master per CiA 302-2. Special case allowed: if OD 0x1F80 == 0x2, a slave may send CO_NMT_ENTER_OPERATIONAL with nodeID 0 to start all nodes.
requirements: Available only when built with NMT master enabled (CO_CONFIG_NMT & CO_CONFIG_NMT_MASTER), except the noted standard exception for slaves (explicit).
nodeID 0 addresses all nodes including self; otherwise addresses the specified node (explicit).
Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success or a CO_ReturnError_t from CO_CANsend on failure (explicit).
NMT must be initialized and have a configured NMT master TX buffer via CO_NMT_init (master variant) (inferred).
Use only where allowed by CiA 302-2; slaves may only send the specified exception (explicit).

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_HBconsumer_init(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, CO_EM_t* em, CO_HBconsNode_t* monitoredNodes, uint8_t monitoredNodesCount, OD_entry_t* OD_1016_HBcons, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdxStart, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initialize a Heartbeat consumer instance and bind it to OD entry 0x1016 and a CAN receive range. Call this during the CANopen communication reset section to set up monitoring of remote node heartbeats. On success, the HBcons object is ready to process incoming heartbeats and track node states; error details may be returned via errInfo.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE is enabled at compile time.
Must be called in the communication reset section (before runtime processing).
HBcons must point to a valid, writable CO_HBconsumer_t object.
em must point to a valid CO_EM_t emergency object.
monitoredNodes must point to an externally defined array of CO_HBconsNode_t entries.
monitoredNodesCount must be in the range 1..127 (inclusive).
OD_1016_HBcons must be a valid OD entry for 0x1016 (Consumer heartbeat time); this entry is required and an IO extension will be applied.
CANdevRx must be a valid CAN device/module used for heartbeat reception.
CANdevRxIdxStart is the starting receive buffer index in CANdevRx; number of used indices equals monitoredNodesCount and must fit the device's RX buffer space.
errInfo is an optional output pointer and may be NULL; when non-NULL it may contain additional error information on failure.
Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; caller must handle other CO_ReturnError_t values.

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackPre(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(void* object));
functions.description: Register an optional pre-processing callback that should promptly trigger CO_HBconsumer_process after a heartbeat CAN frame is received. Useful to wake or signal an OS task to process the consumer immediately.
requirements: Available only when both CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE and CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE are enabled at compile time.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
object is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback and may be NULL.
pFunctSignal may be NULL (disables the callback); when non-NULL it will be invoked after a heartbeat message is received.

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackNmtChanged
functions.signature: void CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackNmtChanged(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, uint8_t idx, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(uint8_t nodeId, uint8_t idx, CO_NMT_internalState_t NMTstate, void* object));
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when a monitored node’s NMT state changes. With MULTI callback support, a separate callback can be set per monitored index.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE is enabled and either CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_CALLBACK_CHANGE or CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_CALLBACK_MULTI is enabled at compile time.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
idx is the node index in the HBcons object; idx is only used when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_CALLBACK_MULTI is enabled.
object is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback and may be NULL.
pFunctSignal may be NULL (disables the callback). When called, parameters are: nodeId of producer, idx, current NMT state, and the user object.

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackHeartbeatStarted
functions.signature: void CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackHeartbeatStarted(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, uint8_t idx, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(uint8_t nodeId, uint8_t idx, void* object));
functions.description: Register a callback fired on the first received heartbeat after enabling the consumer or after a timeout transition back to active. Typically used to wake an external task to handle the event.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE and CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_CALLBACK_MULTI are enabled at compile time.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
idx is the index of the node in the HBcons object.
object is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback and may be NULL.
pFunctSignal may be NULL (disables the callback).

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackTimeout
functions.signature: void CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackTimeout(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, uint8_t idx, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(uint8_t nodeId, uint8_t idx, void* object));
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when a monitored node transitions from active to timeout. Often used to wake or notify an external task of the failure.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE and CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_CALLBACK_MULTI are enabled at compile time.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
idx is the index of the node in the HBcons object.
object is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback and may be NULL.
pFunctSignal may be NULL (disables the callback).

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackRemoteReset
functions.signature: void CO_HBconsumer_initCallbackRemoteReset(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, uint8_t idx, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(uint8_t nodeId, uint8_t idx, void* object));
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when a bootup message (remote reset detected) is received from a monitored node. Typically used to handle remote node resets.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE and CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_CALLBACK_MULTI are enabled at compile time.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
idx is the index of the node in the HBcons object.
object is an opaque user pointer passed to the callback and may be NULL.
pFunctSignal may be NULL (disables the callback).

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_process
functions.signature: void CO_HBconsumer_process(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, bool_t NMTisPreOrOperational, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Run the periodic processing for the Heartbeat consumer. Must be called cyclically to update timeouts, states, and callbacks based on received heartbeats. Provides the next suggested call time via timerNext_us for integration with a scheduler (see CO_process).
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE is enabled at compile time.
Function must be called cyclically during runtime.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
NMTisPreOrOperational must reflect whether the local node is in NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL or NMT_OPERATIONAL state (true) or not (false).
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time since the previous call, in microseconds.
timerNext_us is an output pointer for OS/scheduler hint and must be non-NULL.

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_getIdxByNodeId
functions.signature: int8_t CO_HBconsumer_getIdxByNodeId(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, uint8_t nodeId);
functions.description: Lookup the OD 0x1016 sub-index (internal monitored index) for a given producer node ID. Returns -1 if the node ID is not monitored.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE and CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_QUERY_FUNCT are enabled at compile time.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
nodeId is the producer node ID to search for.
Caller must handle a return value of -1 indicating not found.

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_getState
functions.signature: CO_HBconsumer_state_t CO_HBconsumer_getState(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, uint8_t idx);
functions.description: Get the current heartbeat consumer state for the monitored producer at a given OD 0x1016 sub-index (UNCONFIGURED, UNKNOWN, ACTIVE, or TIMEOUT).
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE and CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_QUERY_FUNCT are enabled at compile time.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
idx must refer to a valid sub-index in OD 0x1016 corresponding to a monitored node.

functions.name: CO_HBconsumer_getNmtState
functions.signature: int8_t CO_HBconsumer_getNmtState(CO_HBconsumer_t* HBcons, uint8_t idx, CO_NMT_internalState_t* nmtState);
functions.description: Retrieve the current NMT state of a monitored producer by OD 0x1016 sub-index. Returns 0 and writes the state when valid; returns -1 when the state is not valid or heartbeat is not enabled for this index.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_ENABLE and CO_CONFIG_HB_CONS_QUERY_FUNCT are enabled at compile time.
HBcons must point to an initialized CO_HBconsumer_t.
idx must refer to a valid sub-index in OD 0x1016 corresponding to a monitored node.
nmtState must be a non-NULL output pointer.
NMT state is only available when heartbeat is enabled for this index; caller must check the return value and only use nmtState when the function returns 0.

functions.name: CO_nodeGuardingSlave_init
functions.signature:
CO_ReturnError_t CO_nodeGuardingSlave_init(CO_nodeGuardingSlave_t* ngs, OD_entry_t* OD_100C_GuardTime,
                                           OD_entry_t* OD_100D_LifeTimeFactor, CO_EM_t* em, uint16_t CANidNodeGuarding,
                                           CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx,
                                           uint16_t CANdevTxIdx, uint32_t* errInfo)
functions.description: Initialize a Node Guarding slave object and bind it to CAN receive/transmit buffers and OD entries for Guard Time (0x100C) and Life Time Factor (0x100D). Use during the CANopen communication reset phase. On success the object is ready to respond to RTR requests from a guarding master and to monitor master presence per configured times.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section.
ngs must be a valid, writable CO_nodeGuardingSlave_t pointer.
OD_100C_GuardTime must reference the required OD entry 0x100C ("Guard time").
OD_100D_LifeTimeFactor must reference the required OD entry 0x100D ("Life time factor").
em must be a valid CO_EM_t emergency object pointer.
CANidNodeGuarding is the CAN identifier for Node Guarding RTR and response (usually CO_CAN_ID_HEARTBEAT + nodeId).
CANdevRx must be a valid CAN device for Node Guarding RTR reception; CANdevRxIdx is the index of its receive buffer.
CANdevTx must be a valid CAN device for Node Guarding response transmission; CANdevTxIdx is the index of its transmit buffer.
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will carry additional error information on failure.
Driver must support RTR identifiers and Node Guarding (per file documentation).
CO_CONFIG_NODE_GUARDING with CO_CONFIG_NODE_GUARDING_SLAVE_ENABLE must be enabled at build time.

functions.name: CO_nodeGuardingSlave_process
functions.signature:
void CO_nodeGuardingSlave_process(CO_nodeGuardingSlave_t* ngs, CO_NMT_internalState_t NMTstate, bool_t slaveDisable,
                                  uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us)
functions.description: Run-time processing for a Node Guarding slave. Call cyclically to handle RTR reception, response transmission, life-time monitoring, and internal timers based on the NMT state and elapsed time.
requirements: Function must be called cyclically.
ngs must be a valid CO_nodeGuardingSlave_t pointer previously initialized by CO_nodeGuardingSlave_init.
NMTstate must be the current NMT operating state provided by the stack.
slaveDisable==true disables Node Guarding slave behavior for this cycle.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; must be accurate and non-negative.
timerNext_us is an output hint for the OS scheduler per CO_process(); usage details are external to this header (nullability not specified).

functions.name: CO_nodeGuardingSlave_isTimeout
functions.signature: static inline bool_t CO_nodeGuardingSlave_isTimeout(CO_nodeGuardingSlave_t* ngs)
functions.description: Query whether the Node Guarding slave has detected a life time timeout (i.e., master RTR not received within the configured life time). The error condition is cleared after the next poll request from the master. Returns true if ngs is NULL or if a timeout has been detected.
requirements: ngs may be NULL; in that case the function returns true by definition.
If ngs is non-NULL, it must point to a CO_nodeGuardingSlave_t previously initialized.
Timeout status is reset after a poll request from master (caller should be aware when interpreting results).

functions.name: CO_nodeGuardingMaster_init
functions.signature:
CO_ReturnError_t CO_nodeGuardingMaster_init(CO_nodeGuardingMaster_t* ngm, CO_EM_t* em, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx,
                                            uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx, uint16_t CANdevTxIdx)
functions.description: Initialize a Node Guarding master object. Binds it to CAN receive and transmit buffers used for receiving slave responses and transmitting RTR polls. Call during the communication reset phase.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section.
ngm must be a valid, writable CO_nodeGuardingMaster_t pointer.
em must be a valid CO_EM_t emergency object pointer.
CANdevRx must be a valid CAN device for Node Guarding reception; CANdevRxIdx is the index of the receive buffer.
CANdevTx must be a valid CAN device for Node Guarding RTR transmission; CANdevTxIdx is the index of the transmit buffer.
CO_CONFIG_NODE_GUARDING with CO_CONFIG_NODE_GUARDING_MASTER_ENABLE must be enabled at build time.
CO_CONFIG_NODE_GUARDING_MASTER_COUNT must be between 1 and 127 inclusive (compile-time).
Driver must support RTR identifiers and Node Guarding (per file documentation).

functions.name: CO_nodeGuardingMaster_initNode
functions.signature:
CO_ReturnError_t CO_nodeGuardingMaster_initNode(CO_nodeGuardingMaster_t* ngm, uint8_t index, uint8_t nodeId,
                                                uint16_t guardTime_ms)
functions.description: Configure monitoring of a specific remote node within a Node Guarding master object. Sets the node’s CAN identifier and guard time. May be called any time after CO_nodeGuardingMaster_init().
requirements: ngm must be a valid CO_nodeGuardingMaster_t pointer previously initialized by CO_nodeGuardingMaster_init.
index must satisfy 0 <= index < CO_CONFIG_NODE_GUARDING_MASTER_COUNT.
nodeId is the Node-ID of the monitored node (CANopen range implicitly 1..127; exact range not specified here).
guardTime_ms is the guard time for the monitored node in milliseconds.
Function may be called any time after CO_nodeGuardingMaster_init().

functions.name: CO_nodeGuardingMaster_process
functions.signature: void CO_nodeGuardingMaster_process(CO_nodeGuardingMaster_t* ngm, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us)
functions.description: Run-time processing for a Node Guarding master. Call cyclically to send RTR polls to configured nodes, receive and interpret responses, maintain toggle/state tracking, and update overall activity/operational flags.
requirements: Function must be called cyclically.
ngm must be a valid CO_nodeGuardingMaster_t pointer previously initialized and with nodes configured as needed.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; must be accurate and non-negative.
timerNext_us is an output hint for the OS scheduler per CO_process(); usage details are external to this header (nullability not specified).

functions.name: CO_EM_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_EM_init(CO_EM_t* em, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx, const OD_entry_t* OD_1001_errReg, CO_EM_fifo_t* fifo, uint8_t fifoSize, OD_entry_t* OD_1014_cobIdEm, uint16_t CANdevTxIdx, OD_entry_t* OD_1015_InhTime, OD_entry_t* OD_1003_preDefErr, OD_entry_t* OD_statusBits, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, const uint8_t nodeId, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initializes the Emergency (EMCY) object for a CANopen node. Must be called during the CANopen communication reset section. Sets up producer/consumer behavior, error history FIFO (0x1003), EMCY COB-ID (0x1014), optional inhibit time (0x1015), error register (0x1001), optional status bits mirroring, and optional consumer reception. When producer/history features are configured and fifoSize >= 2, EMCY events are buffered and later transmitted by CO_EM_process().
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section before using other EM functions.
Parameter em must point to a valid CO_EM_t storage.
Parameter CANdevTx must be a valid, initialized CAN device used for EMCY transmission.
OD_1001_errReg (OD 0x1001) entry is required and must exist without an IO extension.
If EMCY producer or history is enabled, fifo must point to an externally provided buffer with capacity fifoSize and logical capacity (entries) = fifoSize - 1.
fifoSize should usually match length of OD array 0x1003 + 1; if fifoSize < 2, producer and history are disabled and fifo may be NULL.
If EMCY producer is enabled: OD_1014_cobIdEm (OD 0x1014) is required and must have an IO extension; CANdevTxIdx is the transmit buffer index within CANdevTx and must be valid for that device.
If EMCY producer inhibit is enabled: OD_1015_InhTime (OD 0x1015) is optional; IO extension is optional for runtime configuration and may be NULL.
If error history is enabled: OD_1003_preDefErr (OD 0x1003) is optional but if provided must have an IO extension; EM keeps its own memory for this entry.

If status bits exposure is enabled: OD_statusBits is optional but if provided must point to an entry with a subindex 0 variable of size CO_CONFIG_EM_ERR_STATUS_BITS_COUNT/8 bytes and must have an IO extension; EM keeps its own memory for this entry.
If EMCY consumer is enabled: CANdevRx and CANdevRxIdx must specify a valid CAN receive buffer for EMCY reception.
nodeId must be the CANopen node ID of this device (used for default producer).
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives additional error information on failure.
Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; other return values indicate initialization error (details via errInfo when provided).

functions.name: CO_EM_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_EM_initCallbackPre(CO_EM_t* em, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(void* object));
functions.description: Registers an optional pre-callback that is invoked immediately from CO_errorReport()/CO_errorReset() (via CO_error) to trigger timely processing of CO_EM_process() on the mainline. Useful for waking a task to drain the EMCY FIFO promptly.
requirements: em must point to an initialized CO_EM_t.
object is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; it may be NULL.
pFunctSignal may be NULL (no callback will be invoked when NULL).
Callback may be called from any thread/context (including ISR paths), so it should be minimal and safe to trigger a mainline that calls CO_EM_process().

functions.name: CO_EM_initCallbackRx
functions.signature: void CO_EM_initCallbackRx(CO_EM_t* em, void (*pFunctSignalRx)(const uint16_t ident, const uint16_t errorCode, const uint8_t errorRegister, const uint8_t errorBit, const uint32_t infoCode));
functions.description: Registers an optional callback invoked when an EMCY frame is received (or produced locally, signaled by ident == 0). Provides the CAN-ID, error code, error register, error bit index, and info code of the event.
requirements: em must point to an initialized CO_EM_t with EMCY consumer enabled.
pFunctSignalRx may be NULL (no callback will be invoked when NULL).
Depending on CAN driver implementation, the callback may be invoked in an ISR or in the mainline; it must be thread safe and return quickly.

functions.name: CO_EM_process
functions.signature: void CO_EM_process(CO_EM_t* em, bool_t NMTisPreOrOperational, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Cyclically processes the Emergency object. Updates OD 0x1001 (Error register), checks certain communication error conditions, enforces inhibit time, and transmits pending EMCY messages from the FIFO when appropriate.
requirements: Must be called periodically in the mainline/task context.
em must point to an initialized CO_EM_t.
NMTisPreOrOperational must reflect whether the node is in NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL or NMT_OPERATIONAL state (true to allow normal EMCY handling).
timeDifference_us is the time elapsed since the previous call, in microseconds; must be monotonic and accurate enough for inhibit timing.
timerNext_us must be a valid pointer to receive the recommended next call time for scheduling.

functions.name: CO_error
functions.signature: void CO_error(CO_EM_t* em, bool_t setError, const uint8_t errorBit, uint16_t errorCode, uint32_t infoCode);
functions.description: Sets or resets an internal error condition and prepares an EMCY/history entry on state change. If the specified error bit changes state (from clear to set or set to clear), the function enqueues a corresponding EMCY record; CO_EM_process() later transmits it. Designed to be short and thread safe; may be called from any context.
requirements: em should point to an initialized CO_EM_t; function is designed to be callable from any thread/ISR.
errorBit must be within 0..(CO_CONFIG_EM_ERR_STATUS_BITS_COUNT-1) and correspond to a defined error per CO_EM_errorStatusBits_t or manufacturer space.
setError true indicates error occurrence; false indicates resolution/reset.
When resetting (setError == false), errorCode is typically CO_EMC_NO_ERROR; infoCode is a 32-bit optional additional info copied to EMCY bytes 4..7.
If the error bit is already in the requested state (no change), the call is a no-op and no EMCY is generated.

functions.name: CO_isError
functions.signature: static inline bool_t CO_isError(CO_EM_t* em, const uint8_t errorBit);
functions.description: Queries whether a specific error condition is currently active. Returns true if the specified error bit is set. For defensive behavior, it also returns true if em is NULL or errorBit indexes beyond the configured status bits array.
requirements: em should be a valid pointer to CO_EM_t; if em is NULL the function returns true by design.
errorBit is an index from CO_EM_errorStatusBits_t; out-of-range indices cause the function to return true.

functions.name: CO_getErrorRegister
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t CO_getErrorRegister(CO_EM_t* em);
functions.description: Returns the current CANopen Error Register (OD 0x1001). If em or em->errorRegister is NULL, returns 0.
requirements: em should point to a CO_EM_t with errorRegister bound to OD 0x1001; otherwise the function returns 0.

functions.name: CO_errorReport
functions.signature: unknown (CO_errorReport is a macro alias; underlying function is: void CO_error(CO_EM_t* em, bool_t setError, const uint8_t errorBit, uint16_t errorCode, uint32_t infoCode))
functions.description: Macro that reports an error condition by delegating to CO_error(em, true, errorBit, errorCode, infoCode). Purpose: set the specified error status bit and enqueue an Emergency message/history entry on the first transition to error. Usage: call whenever an error condition occurs; CO_EM_process must run cyclically to transmit the prepared Emergency message. Notes: fast and thread-safe; may be called from any thread/ISR. If a pre-callback was registered via CO_EM_initCallbackPre, it is invoked to wake the mainline that calls CO_EM_process.
requirements: em must be a valid, initialized CO_EM_t* obtained via CO_EM_init and remain valid for the call.
errorBit must be a value from CO_EM_errorStatusBits_t and within the configured range [0 .. CO_CONFIG_EM_ERR_STATUS_BITS_COUNT-1].
errorCode must be one of CO_EM_errorCode_t values appropriate to the condition.
infoCode is an optional 32-bit value; if Emergency producer is enabled, it is placed in bytes 4..7 of the EMCY.
An Emergency message is prepared/sent only on a change of the error bit state (i.e., when the bit transitions from 0 to 1).
To actually transmit buffered EMCY messages and update OD 0x1001, CO_EM_process must be called cyclically.

Emergency producer/history transmission requires appropriate CO_CONFIG_EM flags and a fifo size >= 2 with a valid fifo buffer supplied to CO_EM_init; otherwise status bits are still updated but no EMCY/history is produced.
May be called from any thread/ISR; function is thread-safe as documented.

functions.name: CO_errorReset
functions.signature: unknown (CO_errorReset is a macro alias; underlying function is: void CO_error(CO_EM_t* em, bool_t setError, const uint8_t errorBit, uint16_t errorCode, uint32_t infoCode))
functions.description: Macro that clears an error condition by delegating to CO_error(em, false, errorBit, CO_EMC_NO_ERROR, infoCode). Purpose: reset the specified error status bit and enqueue an Emergency message/history entry indicating error reset when the bit transitions to cleared. Usage: call when the previously reported error condition has been resolved; CO_EM_process must run cyclically to transmit the reset Emergency message. Notes: fast and thread-safe; may be called from any thread/ISR. If a pre-callback was registered via CO_EM_initCallbackPre, it is invoked to wake the mainline that calls CO_EM_process.
requirements: em must be a valid, initialized CO_EM_t* obtained via CO_EM_init and remain valid for the call.
errorBit must be a value from CO_EM_errorStatusBits_t and within the configured range [0 .. CO_CONFIG_EM_ERR_STATUS_BITS_COUNT-1].
The macro passes errorCode = CO_EMC_NO_ERROR; callers should not attempt to supply another error code via this macro.
infoCode is an optional 32-bit value; if Emergency producer is enabled, it is placed in bytes 4..7 of the EMCY.
An Emergency reset message is prepared/sent only on a change of the error bit state (i.e., when the bit transitions from 1 to 0).
To actually transmit buffered EMCY messages and update OD 0x1001, CO_EM_process must be called cyclically.

Emergency producer/history transmission requires appropriate CO_CONFIG_EM flags and a fifo size >= 2 with a valid fifo buffer supplied to CO_EM_init; otherwise status bits are still updated but no EMCY/history is produced.
May be called from any thread/ISR; function is thread-safe as documented.

functions.name: CO_SDOserver_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_SDOserver_init(CO_SDOserver_t* SDO, OD_t* OD, OD_entry_t* OD_1200_SDOsrvPar, uint8_t nodeId, uint16_t SDOtimeoutTime_ms, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx, uint16_t CANdevTxIdx, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initialize an SDO server object and bind it to the CANopen Object Dictionary and CAN RX/TX buffers. Call this during the CANopen communication-reset phase to configure the server COB-IDs, timeouts, and CAN resources. Returns a CO_ReturnError_t (CO_ERROR_NO on success). Use OD_1200_SDOsrvPar to support additional SDO server channels or dynamic configuration; for a default single SDO server it can be NULL.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section (before normal operation).
Parameter SDO must be a valid, writable pointer to a CO_SDOserver_t instance.
Parameter OD must be a valid Object Dictionary pointer (OD_t*).
Parameter OD_1200_SDOsrvPar: may be NULL only for the default single SDO server; must not be NULL for additional SDO servers.
If using additional SDO servers with dynamic configuration, OD_1200_SDOsrvPar may have IO extension enabled (per library docs).
Parameter nodeId is used only for the first SDO channel; it is ignored for additional channels.
SDOtimeoutTime_ms specifies the SDO communication timeout in milliseconds; must be a valid application-defined timeout (non-negative, typical positive value).
CANdevRx must point to a valid initialized CO_CANmodule_t used for SDO reception.
CANdevRxIdx must be a valid receive buffer index in CANdevRx.
CANdevTx must point to a valid initialized CO_CANmodule_t used for SDO transmission.
CANdevTxIdx must be a valid transmit buffer index in CANdevTx.
errInfo is an optional output pointer that may be NULL; if non-NULL it is used to provide additional error information on failure.
Function returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; caller should check the return value and handle errors.

functions.name: CO_SDOserver_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_SDOserver_initCallbackPre(CO_SDOserver_t* SDO, void* object, void (*pFunctSignalPre)(void* object));
functions.description: Register an optional pre-processing callback that is invoked when an SDO server message arrives or when immediate processing is required (e.g., during SDO block transfers). Typical usage is to signal or wake the task that calls CO_SDOserver_process(). If pFunctSignalPre is NULL, the callback is disabled.
requirements: This function is only available if compiled with CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE (CO_CONFIG_SDO_SRV includes CO_CONFIG_GLOBAL_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE) or when building documentation; ensure the build configuration enables it.
Parameter SDO must be a valid pointer to an initialized CO_SDOserver_t.
Parameter object is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback; may be NULL.
Parameter pFunctSignalPre is a function pointer taking (void*); may be NULL to disable the callback.

The registered callback should be lightweight and suitable for being called from a CAN receive context or similar ISR/deferred context, as it may be called immediately after an SDO message is received.
Callback should trigger or schedule CO_SDOserver_process() to run without undue delay.

functions.name: CO_SDOserver_process
functions.signature: CO_SDO_return_t CO_SDOserver_process(CO_SDOserver_t* SDO, bool_t NMTisPreOrOperational, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Drive the SDO server state machine. Call this cyclically to process incoming/outgoing SDO transfers, handle timeouts, and manage segmented/block transfers. Returns a CO_SDO_return_t indicating current progress, wait conditions, or completion/abort status. timerNext_us provides the suggested time until the next call (for integration with a scheduler).
requirements: Must be called cyclically during runtime to service the SDO server.
Parameter SDO must be a valid pointer to an initialized CO_SDOserver_t (initialized via CO_SDOserver_init).
Parameter NMTisPreOrOperational should be true only when the NMT state is PRE_OPERATIONAL or OPERATIONAL; pass false otherwise.
Parameter timeDifference_us is the time elapsed since the previous call in microseconds; must be accurate enough to enforce SDO timeouts and non-decreasing per call.
Parameter timerNext_us is an output pointer used to inform the OS/scheduler of the next desired call time; must be a valid writable pointer (not documented as optional).

Caller must handle the returned CO_SDO_return_t: values may indicate waiting for response, buffer full, block transfer in progress, successful end of communication, or aborts; react accordingly (e.g., read buffers, retry later, or handle errors).

functions.name: CO_SDOclient_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_SDOclient_init(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, OD_t* OD, OD_entry_t* OD_1280_SDOcliPar, uint8_t nodeId, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx, uint16_t CANdevTxIdx, uint32_t* errInfo)
functions.description: Initialize an SDO client instance and bind it to CAN RX/TX objects and OD parameters. Must be called during the communication reset phase. If OD_1280_SDOcliPar provides dynamic configuration, the client will use it. Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success or CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid inputs. errInfo may receive additional error information.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section before using the SDO client.
SDO_C must be a valid, writable pointer to CO_SDOclient_t.
OD may be NULL (ignored) if the client will not access its own OD; otherwise must point to a valid Object Dictionary.
OD_1280_SDOcliPar is required (must be a valid pointer to the 0x1280+ SDO client parameter OD entry).
nodeId is the CANopen Node ID of this device; if 0 it is ignored for local OD access.
CANdevRx and CANdevTx must be valid pointers to configured CAN device modules.
CANdevRxIdx and CANdevTxIdx must refer to valid buffers within the respective CAN devices.
errInfo may be NULL if additional error info is not needed.
On return, check the CO_ReturnError_t (CO_ERROR_NO indicates success).

functions.name: CO_SDOclient_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_SDOclient_initCallbackPre(CO_SDOclient_t* SDOclient, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(void* object))
functions.description: Register an optional pre-callback that is invoked when the SDO client receives a CAN frame or when immediate processing is needed (e.g., local exchange or during block transfer). Intended to trigger CO_SDOclientDownload() or CO_SDOclientUpload() processing promptly.
requirements: SDOclient must be a valid, initialized CO_SDOclient_t pointer.
object is an opaque pointer passed to the callback; may be NULL.
pFunctSignal may be NULL (no callback will be invoked if NULL).
Callback should be re-entrant-safe with respect to the application's scheduling model and should promptly schedule or call the non-blocking SDO processing functions.

functions.name: CO_SDOclient_setup
functions.signature: CO_SDO_return_t CO_SDOclient_setup(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, uint32_t COB_IDClientToServer, uint32_t COB_IDServerToClient, uint8_t nodeIDOfTheSDOServer)
functions.description: Configure or reconfigure the SDO client communication parameters (COB-IDs and target server Node-ID). If parameters are unchanged, CAN is not reconfigured. If the server Node-ID equals the local node’s ID, communication will be local (no CAN frames). Returns a CO_SDO_return_t indicating success or wrong arguments.
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid, initialized CO_SDOclient_t pointer (typically after CO_SDOclient_init).
COB_IDClientToServer and COB_IDServerToClient must be valid COB-IDs per CANopen (bit 0..10 CAN-ID, bit 11..30 reserved 0, bit 31 disable flag as described in CO_SDOclient_t).
nodeIDOfTheSDOServer must be a valid CANopen node ID (inferred from naming; exact accepted range not specified in header).
Caller should check the returned CO_SDO_return_t for CO_SDO_RT_ok_communicationEnd or CO_SDO_RT_wrongArguments.

functions.name: CO_SDOclientDownloadInitiate
functions.signature: CO_SDO_return_t CO_SDOclientDownloadInitiate(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, uint16_t index, uint8_t subIndex, size_t sizeIndicated, uint16_t SDOtimeoutTime_ms, bool_t blockEnable)
functions.description: Begin a non-blocking SDO download (client writes to server OD). Optionally indicate the total data size and request block transfer. After initiating, fill the internal buffer via CO_SDOclientDownloadBufWrite() and drive progress with CO_SDOclientDownload().
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid SDO client configured to the intended server (e.g., via CO_SDOclient_setup).
index and subIndex specify the target OD entry on the server; they must be valid for the server (actual validity is server-dependent).
If sizeIndicated != 0, the total bytes written via CO_SDOclientDownloadBufWrite() must equal sizeIndicated; mismatch will abort with an SDO abort code.
SDOtimeoutTime_ms specifies the SDO protocol timeout; choose a value appropriate for the bus/system.
blockEnable requests block transfer; the actual mode depends on server support and negotiation.
Caller must check the returned CO_SDO_return_t and proceed only if initiation succeeded.

functions.name: CO_SDOclientDownloadInitSize
functions.signature: void CO_SDOclientDownloadInitSize(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, size_t sizeIndicated)
functions.description: Optionally update the indicated total download size after initiation if it was not known earlier. Can be used after writing data into the buffer but must be called before CO_SDOclientDownload().
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid SDO client with an ongoing download initiated by CO_SDOclientDownloadInitiate().
Must be called before the first CO_SDOclientDownload() call of the current transfer.
sizeIndicated semantics are the same as in CO_SDOclientDownloadInitiate (0 disables size verification; non-zero enforces exact size).

functions.name: CO_SDOclientDownloadBufWrite
functions.signature: size_t CO_SDOclientDownloadBufWrite(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, const uint8_t* buf, size_t count)
functions.description: Copy application data into the SDO client's internal FIFO buffer for an ongoing or upcoming download. Returns the number of bytes actually written. If the internal buffer lacks space, fewer bytes are copied; the caller may refill later.
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid SDO client object.
buf must be a valid pointer to at least count bytes unless count is 0.
If there is enough space in the destination and sizeIndicated != 0, all data must be written at once (do not split).
May be called multiple times to fill the buffer when space is limited.

functions.name: CO_SDOclientDownload
functions.signature: CO_SDO_return_t CO_SDOclientDownload(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, uint32_t timeDifference_us, bool_t send_abort, bool_t bufferPartial, CO_SDO_abortCode_t* SDOabortCode, size_t* sizeTransferred, uint32_t* timerNext_us)
functions.description: Advance a non-blocking SDO download transfer previously initiated with CO_SDOclientDownloadInitiate(). Call cyclically until it returns <= 0 (error or successful completion). Can accelerate block transfer by repeated immediate calls if the OS CAN TX buffering allows.
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid SDO client with an active download session.
timeDifference_us must be the elapsed time since the previous call, in microseconds.
If send_abort is true, the client sends an abort (using SDOabortCode) and terminates the transfer; SDOabortCode must then point to a valid code.
bufferPartial must be true if not all data have been copied into the internal buffer yet and will be refilled later via CO_SDOclientDownloadBufWrite().
SDOabortCode may be NULL; if non-NULL and the function returns < 0, it holds the abort reason.
sizeTransferred may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the total bytes transferred so far.
timerNext_us may be NULL; if non-NULL, it provides scheduling info for the next call (per CO_process guidance).
Caller must loop calling this function until the return value is <= 0; on < 0, treat as error and session becomes idle; on 0, transfer completed and session becomes idle.
If the return is CO_SDO_RT_blockDownldInProgress and the OS buffers CAN TX, the function may be called multiple times in a tight loop to speed up transfer.

functions.name: CO_SDOclientUploadInitiate
functions.signature: CO_SDO_return_t CO_SDOclientUploadInitiate(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, uint16_t index, uint8_t subIndex, uint16_t SDOtimeoutTime_ms, bool_t blockEnable)
functions.description: Begin a non-blocking SDO upload (client reads from server OD). After initiating, drive progress with CO_SDOclientUpload() and retrieve data from the internal FIFO using CO_SDOclientUploadBufRead().
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid SDO client configured to the intended server (e.g., via CO_SDOclient_setup).
index and subIndex specify the source OD entry on the server; they must be valid for the server (actual validity is server-dependent).
SDOtimeoutTime_ms specifies the SDO protocol timeout; choose a value appropriate for the bus/system.
blockEnable requests block transfer; actual use depends on server support.
Caller must check the returned CO_SDO_return_t and proceed only if initiation succeeded.

functions.name: CO_SDOclientUpload
functions.signature: CO_SDO_return_t CO_SDOclientUpload(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, uint32_t timeDifference_us, bool_t send_abort, CO_SDO_abortCode_t* SDOabortCode, size_t* sizeIndicated, size_t* sizeTransferred, uint32_t* timerNext_us)
functions.description: Advance a non-blocking SDO upload session initiated with CO_SDOclientUploadInitiate(). Call cyclically until it returns <= 0 (error or successful completion). When the internal FIFO becomes full, read data out with CO_SDOclientUploadBufRead() and call again. Do not read from the FIFO while block upload is in progress.
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid SDO client with an active upload session.
timeDifference_us must be the elapsed time since the previous call, in microseconds.
If send_abort is true, the client sends an abort (using SDOabortCode) and terminates the transfer; SDOabortCode must then point to a valid code.
SDOabortCode may be NULL; if non-NULL and the function returns < 0, it holds the abort reason.

If the function returns CO_SDO_RT_uploadDataBufferFull, the caller must drain data from the FIFO (via CO_SDOclientUploadBufRead()) and can call this function again immediately to speed up block transfer.
Do not read data from the FIFO when the function returns CO_SDO_RT_blockUploadInProgress.
sizeIndicated may be NULL; if non-NULL and > 0, the server indicated total transfer size.
sizeTransferred may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives the total bytes transferred so far.
timerNext_us may be NULL; if non-NULL, it provides scheduling info for the next call (per CO_process guidance).
Caller must loop calling this function until the return value is <= 0; on < 0, treat as error and session becomes idle; on 0, transfer completed and session becomes idle.

functions.name: CO_SDOclientUploadBufRead
functions.signature: size_t CO_SDOclientUploadBufRead(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, uint8_t* buf, size_t count)
functions.description: Copy received data from the SDO client’s internal FIFO into the user buffer. Can be called repeatedly to retrieve long transfers. Must not be called while CO_SDOclientUpload() reports block upload in progress.
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid SDO client object with data available in its FIFO (as produced by CO_SDOclientUpload()).
buf must be a valid pointer to at least count bytes unless count is 0.
Must NOT be called when CO_SDOclientUpload() returns CO_SDO_RT_blockUploadInProgress.
May be called multiple times until all data are drained; it returns the number of bytes actually copied.

functions.name: CO_SDOclientClose
functions.signature: void CO_SDOclientClose(CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C)
functions.description: Temporarily close SDO communication for this client. Disables reception of SDO client CAN messages to prevent writes into undefined buffers after a transfer completes. Should be called after each SDO client communication cycle finishes.
requirements: SDO_C must be a valid SDO client object.
Must be called after finishing each SDO client communication cycle to disable SDO RX and avoid undefined buffer writes.

functions.name: CO_SYNC_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_SYNC_init(CO_SYNC_t* SYNC, CO_EM_t* em, OD_entry_t* OD_1005_cobIdSync, OD_entry_t* OD_1006_commCyclePeriod, OD_entry_t* OD_1007_syncWindowLen, OD_entry_t* OD_1019_syncCounterOvf, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx, uint16_t CANdevTxIdx, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initializes the CANopen SYNC producer/consumer object. Must be called during the communication reset section. Binds SYNC to Object Dictionary entries (0x1005, 0x1006, 0x1007, 0x1019) and configures CAN reception and (if producer) transmission resources. Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; otherwise an error code and optionally errInfo. Use this signature when the device is configured as a SYNC producer (producer configuration enables TX parameters).
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section before using SYNC or related PDO processing.
SYNC must be a valid, writable CO_SYNC_t pointer.
em must be a valid CO_EM_t pointer (emergency object).
OD_1005_cobIdSync (OD 0x1005) is required and must be a valid OD_entry_t pointer.
OD_1006_commCyclePeriod (OD 0x1006) is required for SYNC producer devices and must be a valid OD_entry_t pointer in that case.
OD_1007_syncWindowLen (OD 0x1007) is optional and may be NULL.
OD_1019_syncCounterOvf (OD 0x1019) is optional and may be NULL.
CANdevRx must be a valid CO_CANmodule_t pointer and CANdevRxIdx must reference a valid receive buffer in that module.
CANdevTx must be a valid CO_CANmodule_t pointer and CANdevTxIdx must reference a valid transmit buffer in that module (producer configuration).
errInfo is an optional output pointer and may be NULL; if non-NULL it may receive additional error information on failure.
Caller should check the returned CO_ReturnError_t and handle errors; success is indicated by CO_ERROR_NO.

functions.name: CO_SYNC_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_SYNC_initCallbackPre(CO_SYNC_t* SYNC, void* object, void (*pFunctSignalPre)(void* object));
functions.description: Registers an optional pre-processing callback invoked immediately after a SYNC message is received from the CAN bus. Intended to signal the application to promptly call CO_SYNC_process(). If pFunctSignalPre is NULL, no callback is invoked.
requirements: This function is available only when CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE for SYNC is enabled at build time.
SYNC must be a valid, previously initialized CO_SYNC_t pointer.
object is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback; may be NULL if the callback does not need context.
pFunctSignalPre may be NULL to disable the callback; if non-NULL it must be callable at interrupt or callback context as appropriate for CAN RX handling.

functions.name: CO_SYNCsend
functions.signature: static inline CO_ReturnError_t CO_SYNCsend(CO_SYNC_t* SYNC);
functions.description: Immediately prepares and transmits a SYNC message. Increments and wraps the SYNC counter according to 0x1019, resets the SYNC timer, toggles the internal RX/TX toggle, writes the counter into CAN data byte 0 when enabled, and sends via CO_CANsend(). Use this only when the application needs direct control of SYNC transmission; otherwise prefer CO_SYNC_process(). Returns the result of CO_CANsend().
requirements: Available only when SYNC producer support is enabled at build time (CO_CONFIG_SYNC_PRODUCER).
SYNC must be a valid, initialized producer object (isProducer true) with CANdevTx and CANtxBuff configured by CO_SYNC_init().
The Object Dictionary 0x1019 (counter overflow) controls counter behavior; if zero, counter byte may be unused by configuration.
Caller must handle the returned CO_ReturnError_t from CO_CANsend().
Should not be called concurrently with CO_SYNC_process() unless the application guarantees proper synchronization (reentrancy and concurrency are not specified).

functions.name: CO_SYNC_process
functions.signature: CO_SYNC_status_t CO_SYNC_process(CO_SYNC_t* SYNC, bool_t NMTisPreOrOperational, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Processes SYNC producer/consumer state. Must be called cyclically. Handles SYNC reception/transmission timing based on OD 0x1006 (communication cycle period) and 0x1007 (synchronous window length), updates timing state, and reports whether a SYNC was received/transmitted or the window just passed. Writes the recommended time until next invocation to timerNext_us.
requirements: Must be called cyclically; pass the elapsed time since the previous call in timeDifference_us (microseconds).
SYNC must be a valid, initialized CO_SYNC_t pointer.
NMTisPreOrOperational must reflect whether the node is in NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL or NMT_OPERATIONAL state.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the prior call (uint32_t range).
timerNext_us must be a valid, writable pointer for receiving the suggested next call time; not documented as optional, so it should not be NULL.
Caller should handle the returned CO_SYNC_status_t to react to SYNC events (none, rx/tx occurred, or window passed).

functions.name: CO_RPDO_init
functions.signature:
CO_ReturnError_t CO_RPDO_init(CO_RPDO_t* RPDO, OD_t* OD, CO_EM_t* em,
#if (((CO_CONFIG_PDO)&CO_CONFIG_PDO_SYNC_ENABLE) != 0) || defined CO_DOXYGEN
                              CO_SYNC_t* SYNC,
#endif
                              uint16_t preDefinedCanId, OD_entry_t* OD_14xx_RPDOCommPar, OD_entry_t* OD_16xx_RPDOMapPar,
                              CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initialize an RPDO (Receive PDO) object and bind it to Object Dictionary entries, CAN receive resources, and optional SYNC. Intended to be called at the end of the communication-reset section, after the application and OD are initialized, so that PDO mappings resolve correctly. Returns a CANopen error code via CO_ReturnError_t and may provide additional error info via errInfo.
requirements: Call at the end of the communication reset section, after all application initialization is complete.
Parameter RPDO must be a valid, writable CO_RPDO_t instance.
Parameter OD must be a valid Object Dictionary instance (OD_t*).
Parameter em must be a valid Emergency object (CO_EM_t*).
If CO_CONFIG_PDO_SYNC_ENABLE is enabled, SYNC may be provided or set to NULL; if disabled, SYNC parameter is not present.
preDefinedCanId is either a pre-defined connection-set CAN-ID (including node-id for the first four PDOs) or 0 for none.
OD_14xx_RPDOCommPar must reference the required OD entry 0x1400+ (RPDO communication parameter).
OD_16xx_RPDOMapPar must reference the required OD entry 0x1600+ (RPDO mapping parameter).
CANdevRx must be a valid CAN device for reception; CANdevRxIdx must select a valid receive buffer within that device.
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL, it may receive additional error detail.
Function returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; caller should handle other CO_ReturnError_t values appropriately.

functions.name: CO_RPDO_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_RPDO_initCallbackPre(CO_RPDO_t* RPDO, void* object, void (*pFunctSignalPre)(void* object));
functions.description: Register an optional pre-callback for an RPDO that is invoked immediately after an RPDO frame is received from the CAN bus. Intended to trigger prompt processing (e.g., waking a task that calls CO_RPDO_process).
requirements: RPDO must be a valid, initialized CO_RPDO_t instance from CO_RPDO_init.
object is an opaque pointer passed to the callback when invoked; no constraints.
pFunctSignalPre may be NULL to disable the callback; if non-NULL it must be callable and quick (should only signal/trigger CO_RPDO_process).
Callback is invoked from the context that handles CAN reception; it should not block or perform heavy processing.

functions.name: CO_RPDO_process
functions.signature:
void CO_RPDO_process(CO_RPDO_t* RPDO,
#if (((CO_CONFIG_PDO)&CO_CONFIG_RPDO_TIMERS_ENABLE) != 0) || defined CO_DOXYGEN
                     uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us,
#endif
                     bool_t NMTisOperational, bool_t syncWas);
functions.description: Process received RPDO messages and copy mapped data into OD variables when appropriate. Should be called cyclically in any NMT state; performs updates when new PDOs were received, the PDO is valid, and the node is operational. Synchronous RPDOs are applied after the next SYNC.
requirements: Call cyclically in any NMT state.
RPDO must be a valid, initialized CO_RPDO_t instance.
If CO_CONFIG_PDO_RPDO_TIMERS_ENABLE is enabled, provide timeDifference_us since the previous call (in microseconds) and a non-NULL timerNext_us pointer for OS scheduling feedback.
NMTisOperational must reflect whether the node is currently in NMT_OPERATIONAL state.
syncWas must be true if a SYNC was just received/transmitted; affects processing of synchronous RPDOs.

functions.name: CO_TPDO_init
functions.signature:
CO_ReturnError_t CO_TPDO_init(CO_TPDO_t* TPDO, OD_t* OD, CO_EM_t* em,
#if (((CO_CONFIG_PDO)&CO_CONFIG_PDO_SYNC_ENABLE) != 0) || defined CO_DOXYGEN
                              CO_SYNC_t* SYNC,
#endif
                              uint16_t preDefinedCanId, OD_entry_t* OD_18xx_TPDOCommPar, OD_entry_t* OD_1Axx_TPDOMapPar,
                              CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx, uint16_t CANdevTxIdx, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initialize a TPDO (Transmit PDO) object and bind it to Object Dictionary entries, a CAN transmit buffer, and optional SYNC. Intended to be called at the end of the communication-reset section, after OD and application initialization, to ensure correct PDO mapping. Returns a CANopen error via CO_ReturnError_t and may fill errInfo with additional detail.
requirements: Call at the end of the communication reset section, after all application initialization is complete.
Parameter TPDO must be a valid, writable CO_TPDO_t instance.
Parameter OD must be a valid Object Dictionary instance (OD_t*).
Parameter em must be a valid Emergency object (CO_EM_t*).
If CO_CONFIG_PDO_SYNC_ENABLE is enabled, SYNC may be provided or set to NULL; if disabled, SYNC parameter is not present.
preDefinedCanId is either a pre-defined connection-set CAN-ID (including node-id for the first four PDOs) or 0 for none.
OD_18xx_TPDOCommPar must reference the required OD entry 0x1800+ (TPDO communication parameter).
OD_1Axx_TPDOMapPar must reference the required OD entry 0x1A00+ (TPDO mapping parameter).
CANdevTx must be a valid CAN device for transmission; CANdevTxIdx must select a valid transmit buffer within that device.
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL, it may receive additional error detail.
Function returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; caller should handle other CO_ReturnError_t values appropriately.

functions.name: CO_TPDOsendRequest
functions.signature: static inline void CO_TPDOsendRequest(CO_TPDO_t* TPDO);
functions.description: Request transmission of a TPDO. For transmission types 0, 254, or 255 (event-driven), CO_TPDO_process will transmit the PDO after any inhibit time expires. Safe to call with a NULL pointer (the function checks and does nothing).
requirements: TPDO may be NULL; if NULL the function performs no action.
For the request to lead to transmission, the TPDO must be configured with transmission type 0, 254, or 255 and be otherwise valid/enabled.
Actual sending occurs inside CO_TPDO_process after inhibit timing constraints are satisfied.

functions.name: CO_TPDO_process
functions.signature:
void CO_TPDO_process(CO_TPDO_t* TPDO,
#if (((CO_CONFIG_PDO)&CO_CONFIG_TPDO_TIMERS_ENABLE) != 0) || defined CO_DOXYGEN
                     uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us,
#endif
                     bool_t NMTisOperational, bool_t syncWas);
functions.description: Prepare and transmit TPDOs as required by mapping, transmission type, timing (inhibit/event), SYNC, and send requests. Should be called cyclically in any NMT state.
requirements: Call cyclically in any NMT state.
TPDO must be a valid, initialized CO_TPDO_t instance.
If CO_CONFIG_PDO_TPDO_TIMERS_ENABLE is enabled, provide timeDifference_us since the previous call (in microseconds) and a non-NULL timerNext_us pointer for OS scheduling feedback.
NMTisOperational must reflect whether the node is currently in NMT_OPERATIONAL state.
syncWas must be true if a SYNC was just received/transmitted; affects synchronous TPDO behavior.
If using CO_TPDOsendRequest or OD_requestTPDO, expect transmission only when inhibit timer permits and per transmission type rules.

functions.name: CO_TIME_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_TIME_init(CO_TIME_t* TIME, OD_entry_t* OD_1012_cobIdTimeStamp, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initializes a CANopen TIME (timestamp) object for a TIME consumer-only configuration. Must be called during the communication reset section. Binds the TIME object to the OD entry 0x1012 (COB-ID time stamp) and configures CAN reception. On success returns CO_ERROR_NO.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section (before normal operation).
TIME must point to a valid CO_TIME_t instance to be initialized.
OD_1012_cobIdTimeStamp must be a valid OD entry for index 0x1012 (required).
CANdevRx must be a valid, initialized CAN device/module for TIME reception.
CANdevRxIdx must refer to a valid receive buffer/index within CANdevRx.
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL, it receives additional error information.
Caller must check the returned CO_ReturnError_t for success (CO_ERROR_NO) or failure.
Function availability and behavior assume TIME producer functionality is disabled at compile time (no Tx parameters).

functions.name: CO_TIME_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_TIME_initCallbackPre(CO_TIME_t* TIME, void* object, void (*pFunctSignalPre)(void* object));
functions.description: Registers an optional pre-callback to be invoked immediately after a TIME message is received. Intended to promptly trigger processing of CO_TIME_process() when a new TIME frame arrives.
requirements: TIME must point to a valid CO_TIME_t object (typically after CO_TIME_init).
object is an opaque pointer passed back to pFunctSignalPre when invoked; may be NULL if unused.
pFunctSignalPre may be NULL (no callback will be called in that case).
Callback will be called after a TIME message is received from the CAN bus.
Available only when global pre-callback support is enabled at compile time.

functions.name: CO_TIME_set
functions.signature: static inline void CO_TIME_set(CO_TIME_t* TIME, uint32_t ms, uint16_t days, uint32_t producerInterval_ms);
functions.description: Sets the current time in the TIME object. For producer-enabled builds, also sets the producer interval and resets the producer timer so TIME frames will be sent periodically from CO_TIME_process().
requirements: TIME may be NULL; in that case the function does nothing.
ms is interpreted as milliseconds after midnight (no range is enforced by this function).
days is interpreted as number of days since January 1, 1984 (no range is enforced by this function).
In producer-enabled builds, producerInterval_ms configures the periodic transmit interval; in consumer-only builds it is ignored.
If the node acts as TIME producer, this should be called at least once to establish the initial time and interval (per module documentation).

functions.name: CO_TIME_process
functions.signature: bool_t CO_TIME_process(CO_TIME_t* TIME, bool_t NMTisPreOrOperational, uint32_t timeDifference_us);
functions.description: Periodically processes the TIME object. Updates internal time using either received TIME messages or the supplied elapsed time, and, if configured as a producer with a set interval, transmits TIME messages. Returns true if a new TIME message was recently received (consumer).
requirements: Must be called cyclically during runtime.
TIME must point to a valid, initialized CO_TIME_t object.
timeDifference_us must be the time elapsed since the previous call, in microseconds.
NMTisPreOrOperational must be true when the node is in NMT_PRE_OPERATIONAL or NMT_OPERATIONAL state; pass false otherwise.
Producer timestamp transmission requires producer mode enabled and a non-zero producer interval to have been set (e.g., via CO_TIME_set).

functions.name: CO_fifo_init
functions.signature: void CO_fifo_init(CO_fifo_t* fifo, uint8_t* buf, size_t bufSize)
functions.description: Initialize a FIFO circular buffer object with an external byte buffer. Usable capacity is bufSize - 1 to enable wrap-around semantics. Call this before other FIFO operations.
requirements: fifo must not be NULL.
buf must not be NULL.
bufSize must be greater than 1 (usable capacity is bufSize - 1).
The memory pointed to by buf must remain valid for the lifetime of the fifo usage.
Functions are not thread safe; callers must serialize access if used concurrently.

functions.name: CO_fifo_reset
functions.signature: static inline void CO_fifo_reset(CO_fifo_t* fifo)
functions.description: Reset the FIFO to empty state by setting read and write pointers to zero. If ASCII datatypes support is enabled, also clears the internal 'started' flag. Intended to clear contents without reinitializing buffer configuration.
requirements: fifo must not be NULL.
FIFO should have been initialized with CO_fifo_init() prior to reset.

functions.name: CO_fifo_purge
functions.signature: static inline bool_t CO_fifo_purge(CO_fifo_t* fifo)
functions.description: Purge all data in the FIFO (set read and write pointers to zero) and keep other properties. Returns true if data were purged, false if FIFO was already empty or fifo is NULL.
requirements: fifo must not be NULL for a meaningful operation.
FIFO should have been initialized with CO_fifo_init() prior to purge.

functions.name: CO_fifo_getSpace
functions.signature: static inline size_t CO_fifo_getSpace(CO_fifo_t* fifo)
functions.description: Return the number of free bytes available for writing in the FIFO (accounting for circular buffer semantics, leaving one byte unused).
requirements: fifo must not be NULL and must have been initialized (bufSize must be valid).

functions.name: CO_fifo_getOccupied
functions.signature: static inline size_t CO_fifo_getOccupied(CO_fifo_t* fifo)
functions.description: Return the number of bytes currently stored in the FIFO (readable without overwriting).
requirements: fifo must not be NULL and must have been initialized (bufSize must be valid).

functions.name: CO_fifo_putc
functions.signature: static inline bool_t CO_fifo_putc(CO_fifo_t* fifo, const uint8_t c)
functions.description: Attempt to write a single byte to the FIFO without overwriting existing data. Returns true on success, false if FIFO is full or inputs are invalid.
requirements: fifo must not be NULL.
fifo->buf must not be NULL (FIFO must be initialized).
There must be at least one byte of free space; otherwise function returns false.

functions.name: CO_fifo_putc_ov
functions.signature: static inline void CO_fifo_putc_ov(CO_fifo_t* fifo, const uint8_t c)
functions.description: Write a single byte to the FIFO, overwriting the oldest data if the buffer is full. Always advances write pointer; if this causes overlap with read pointer, the read pointer advances (oldest byte dropped).
requirements: fifo must not be NULL.
fifo->buf must not be NULL (FIFO must be initialized).
Caller must tolerate loss of oldest data when buffer is full (function overwrites).

functions.name: CO_fifo_getc
functions.signature: static inline bool_t CO_fifo_getc(CO_fifo_t* fifo, uint8_t* buf)
functions.description: Read one byte from the FIFO into the provided buffer. Returns true if a byte was read, false if FIFO is empty or inputs are invalid.
requirements: fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
buf must not be NULL.
There must be at least one byte available to read; otherwise function returns false.

functions.name: CO_fifo_write
functions.signature: size_t CO_fifo_write(CO_fifo_t* fifo, const uint8_t* buf, size_t count, uint16_t* crc)
functions.description: Copy up to count bytes from buf into the FIFO, stopping early if there is not enough free space. Optionally updates an external CRC accumulator if crc is not NULL. Returns the number of bytes actually written.
requirements: fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized with a valid buffer.
If count > 0 then buf must not be NULL.
crc may be NULL to skip CRC accumulation.

functions.name: CO_fifo_read
functions.signature: size_t CO_fifo_read(CO_fifo_t* fifo, uint8_t* buf, size_t count, bool_t* eof)
functions.description: Copy up to count bytes from the FIFO into buf. Returns the number of bytes actually read. If eof is not NULL, the function searches for a command delimiter; if found, it reads through that delimiter and sets *eof to true, otherwise sets *eof to false. Details of the delimiter depend on configuration (not specified here).
requirements: fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
buf must not be NULL if count > 0.
eof may be NULL to skip delimiter detection.
Delimiter value/handling is configuration-dependent and not specified in this header; callers relying on eof must ensure proper delimiter configuration elsewhere.

functions.name: CO_fifo_altBegin
functions.signature: size_t CO_fifo_altBegin(CO_fifo_t* fifo, size_t offset)
functions.description: Initialize an alternate read position starting at an offset from the main read pointer, for lookahead-style reading. Returns the effective offset applied (may be smaller if not enough data).
requirements: Feature CO_CONFIG_FIFO_ALT_READ must be enabled at compile time.
fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
offset should be within the available occupied data; if larger, it will be reduced to available data.

functions.name: CO_fifo_altFinish
functions.signature: void CO_fifo_altFinish(CO_fifo_t* fifo, uint16_t* crc)
functions.description: Finish alternate reading by committing the main read pointer to the alternate read pointer, effectively consuming the alternately-read data. Optionally updates an external CRC accumulator if crc is not NULL.
requirements: Feature CO_CONFIG_FIFO_ALT_READ must be enabled at compile time.
fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
Should be called after CO_fifo_altBegin() and any CO_fifo_altRead() usage to commit, if commit is desired.
crc may be NULL to skip CRC accumulation.

functions.name: CO_fifo_altGetOccupied
functions.signature: static inline size_t CO_fifo_altGetOccupied(CO_fifo_t* fifo)
functions.description: Return the number of bytes available to read from the current alternate read pointer up to the write pointer.
requirements: Feature CO_CONFIG_FIFO_ALT_READ must be enabled at compile time.
fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
Alternate read pointer should have been set with CO_fifo_altBegin() to have meaningful results.

functions.name: CO_fifo_altRead
functions.signature: size_t CO_fifo_altRead(CO_fifo_t* fifo, uint8_t* buf, size_t count)
functions.description: Read up to count bytes from the FIFO using the alternate read pointer without consuming data from the main read pointer. Returns number of bytes read. Use CO_fifo_altFinish() to commit alternate progress if desired.
requirements: Feature CO_CONFIG_FIFO_ALT_READ must be enabled at compile time.
fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
CO_fifo_altBegin() must have been called to set the alternate read pointer before using this function.
buf must not be NULL if count > 0.

functions.name: CO_fifo_CommSearch
functions.signature: bool_t CO_fifo_CommSearch(CO_fifo_t* fifo, bool_t clear)
functions.description: Search the FIFO for a complete command delimited by a configured command delimiter. If the buffer is full and no delimiter is present (long command), returns true to allow processing of starting tokens; subsequent refills can complete the command. If a command with delimiter is found or buffer is full, returns true. If clear is true, the found command (or entire buffer if no delimiter) is cleared.
requirements: Feature CO_CONFIG_FIFO_ASCII_COMMANDS must be enabled at compile time.
fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
Caller should process tokens and handle errors in a single higher-level function call as suggested by the comments.
If clear is true, caller must be prepared that data in the buffer will be removed (either the command or the whole buffer if no delimiter).

functions.name: CO_fifo_trimSpaces
functions.signature: bool_t CO_fifo_trimSpaces(CO_fifo_t* fifo, bool_t* insideComment)
functions.description: Remove all non-graphical characters and comments from the FIFO, stopping at the first graphical character or command delimiter (the delimiter is also removed). Returns true if a command delimiter was found. insideComment is an in/out flag: if true on input, the function skips characters searching only for the delimiter; on output it is set to true if FIFO is empty, currently inside a comment, and no delimiter was found.
requirements: Feature CO_CONFIG_FIFO_ASCII_COMMANDS must be enabled at compile time.
fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
insideComment must not be NULL (used as in/out parameter).

functions.name: CO_fifo_readToken
functions.signature: size_t CO_fifo_readToken(CO_fifo_t* fifo, char* buf, size_t count, uint8_t* closed, bool_t* err)
functions.description: Extract the next token from the FIFO. A token is a string of graphical characters (0x21–0x7E). Copies the token to buf (NUL-terminated) if count allows. Sets the read pointer to the next graphical character on success. If a comment delimiter is encountered, content up to the command delimiter is erased. If closed is provided, it is set to 1 if the command delimiter follows the token, else 0. If closed is provided as input with 0 or 1, the function sets *err to true for specific mismatches (empty token or unexpected/missing delimiter). Returns the number of bytes read into buf.
requirements: Feature CO_CONFIG_FIFO_ASCII_COMMANDS must be enabled at compile time.
fifo must not be NULL and must be initialized.
buf must not be NULL. Buffer must have sufficient size (count) to hold the token plus NUL terminator, otherwise an error is indicated via err.
count specifies the maximum bytes to copy including space for the terminating '\0'.
closed may be NULL if delimiter status is not needed; if provided, its incoming value affects error checking as documented.
err may be NULL; if provided and already true on entry, the function returns immediately.

functions.name: crc16_ccitt_single
functions.signature: void crc16_ccitt_single(uint16_t* crc, const uint8_t chr);
functions.description: Updates a running CRC-16/CCITT checksum with a single data byte. Typical usage is to initialize the CRC to a known value (zero for XMODEM variant), then call this function for each byte to accumulate the checksum in place via the crc pointer.
requirements: crc must be a valid, non-null pointer to a writable uint16_t.
Before starting a new CRC calculation, *crc must be initialized; use 0 for XMODEM-style initialization.
chr is a single data byte (0..255).
Function availability depends on build-time configuration: it is only compiled when CO_CONFIG_CRC16 has CO_CONFIG_CRC16_ENABLE set (or CO_DOXYGEN is defined).

functions.name: crc16_ccitt
functions.signature: uint16_t crc16_ccitt(const uint8_t block[], size_t blockLength, uint16_t crc);
functions.description: Computes the CRC-16/CCITT checksum over a block of bytes. Can be used for one-shot calculation or continued across segments by passing the previous CRC as the crc parameter (initialize to 0 for XMODEM variant). Returns the resulting 16-bit CRC.
requirements: block must point to a memory region containing at least blockLength bytes that is readable for the duration of the call.
blockLength specifies the number of bytes to process; it must not exceed the actual accessible size of block.
crc provides the initial CRC value; for multi-segment processing, pass the CRC returned from the prior call; for XMODEM initialization, use 0.
Function availability depends on build-time configuration: it is only compiled when CO_CONFIG_CRC16 has CO_CONFIG_CRC16_ENABLE set (or CO_DOXYGEN is defined).

requirements: This function is available only if CO_CONFIG_LEDS_ENABLE is enabled at compile time.
