Caller must check the return value and handle CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT.

functions.name: CO_LEDs_process
functions.signature: void CO_LEDs_process(CO_LEDs_t* LEDs, uint32_t timeDifference_us, CO_NMT_internalState_t NMTstate, bool_t LSSconfig, bool_t ErrCANbusOff, bool_t ErrCANbusWarn, bool_t ErrRpdo, bool_t ErrSync, bool_t ErrHbCons, bool_t ErrOther, bool_t firmwareDownload, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Updates the LED indicator state machine (green and red) according to CiA 303-3 based on current NMT state and error indications. Must be called cyclically with the elapsed time since the previous call; it computes the flicker/blink/flash patterns and writes next recommended call deadline via timerNext_us (see CO_process()).
requirements: This function is available only if CO_CONFIG_LEDS_ENABLE is enabled at compile time.
LEDs must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to an initialized CO_LEDs_t (initialized via CO_LEDs_init).
Call this function cyclically; timeDifference_us should represent the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call (must fit in uint32_t).
NMTstate must be a valid CO_NMT_internalState_t value.
timerNext_us must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to uint32_t that the function can write to.
Boolean indication parameters (LSSconfig, ErrCANbusOff, ErrCANbusWarn, ErrRpdo, ErrSync, ErrHbCons, ErrOther, firmwareDownload) should reflect the current device status at the time of the call.
Do not call before CO_LEDs_init has successfully completed.

functions.name: CO_GFC_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_GFC_init(CO_GFC_t* GFC, OD_entry_t* OD_1300_gfcParameter, CO_CANmodule_t* GFC_CANdevRx, uint16_t GFC_rxIdx, uint16_t CANidRxGFC, CO_CANmodule_t* GFC_CANdevTx, uint16_t GFC_txIdx, uint16_t CANidTxGFC)
functions.description: Initializes a Global fail-safe command (GFC) object, binding it to the Object Dictionary entry 0x1300 and configuring CAN reception/transmission resources for GFC messages. Use this during the CANopen communication reset phase to set up the GFC consumer and/or producer according to the build-time configuration. On success, the object is ready to receive GFC frames and/or send a GFC frame with ID 1/DLC 0 (per protocol); specific CAN-IDs for Rx/Tx are provided by the caller.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section before using the GFC object.
GFC must be a valid, writable pointer to a CO_GFC_t instance.
OD_1300_gfcParameter must point to the Object Dictionary entry for index 0x1300 (Global fail-safe command parameter).
GFC_CANdevRx must be a valid CAN module handle for receiving GFC (if consumer functionality is enabled).
GFC_rxIdx must be a valid receive buffer index within GFC_CANdevRx (range depends on the CAN driver; unknown exact limits).
CANidRxGFC must be the CAN identifier to subscribe for GFC reception (exact valid range depends on CAN configuration; unknown).
GFC_CANdevTx must be a valid CAN module handle for transmitting GFC (if producer functionality is enabled).
GFC_txIdx must be a valid transmit buffer index within GFC_CANdevTx (range depends on the CAN driver; unknown exact limits).
CANidTxGFC must be the CAN identifier to use for GFC transmission (exact valid range depends on CAN configuration; unknown).
Function availability and behavior depend on CO_CONFIG_GFC being enabled at compile time; producer/consumer specifics require their respective flags.
On error, returns CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT; on success, returns CO_ERROR_NO.

functions.name: CO_GFC_initCallbackEnterSafeState
functions.signature: void CO_GFC_initCallbackEnterSafeState(CO_GFC_t* GFC, void* object, void (*pFunctSignalSafe)(void* object))
functions.description: Registers an optional callback that is invoked when a GFC message is received. The callback is called from the receive path (interrupt context) and can be used to begin transitioning the application to a safe state upon GFC reception.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_GFC enables consumer functionality at compile time.
GFC must point to an initialized CO_GFC_t (initialized by CO_GFC_init).
object is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; it may be NULL.
pFunctSignalSafe may be NULL (no callback will be invoked if NULL).
Callback runs in interrupt context; it must be ISR-safe, fast, non-blocking, and must not call functions that are unsafe in ISRs (exact constraints depend on the platform; unknown).

functions.name: CO_GFCsend
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_GFCsend(CO_GFC_t* GFC)
functions.description: Sends a GFC message (ID 1, DLC 0 per protocol) to notify consumers of a safety-relevant change. Typically called by the application when entering or commanding a fail-safe condition.
requirements: Available only when CO_CONFIG_GFC enables producer functionality at compile time.
GFC must point to an initialized CO_GFC_t (initialized by CO_GFC_init with valid transmit configuration).
Returns the same status codes as CO_CANsend() (exact set of codes depends on the CAN driver; unknown).
Caller should ensure transmit CAN resources are operational before calling (e.g., CAN module started; specific preconditions depend on the platform; unknown).

functions.name: CO_SRDOGuard_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_SRDOGuard_init(CO_SRDOGuard_t* SRDOGuard, OD_entry_t* OD_13FE_configurationValid, OD_entry_t* OD_13FF_safetyConfigurationSignature, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initialize the SRDO guard object that supervises SRDO configuration validity, CRC objects access, and NMT operational changes. Must be invoked in the communication reset phase before any CO_SRDO_init() calls. On success it wires OD 0x13FE (Configuration valid) and 0x13FF (Safety configuration signature) entries and prepares internal OD I/O hooks.
requirements: Call during the communication reset section, before CO_SRDO_init().
SRDOGuard must point to writable, uninitialized or re-initializable CO_SRDOGuard_t storage.
OD_13FE_configurationValid must reference OD entry 0x13FE:00 (Configuration valid).
OD_13FF_safetyConfigurationSignature must reference OD entry 0x13FF:00 (Safety configuration signature).
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL it is written with additional error information on failure.
Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; may return CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid inputs.

functions.name: CO_SRDO_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_SRDO_init(CO_SRDO_t* SRDO, uint8_t SRDO_Index, CO_SRDOGuard_t* SRDOGuard, OD_t* OD, CO_EM_t* em, uint8_t nodeId, uint16_t defaultCOB_ID, OD_entry_t* OD_130x_SRDOCommPar, OD_entry_t* OD_138x_SRDOMapPar, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRxNormal, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRxInverted, uint16_t CANdevRxIdxNormal, uint16_t CANdevRxIdxInverted, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTxNormal, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTxInverted, uint16_t CANdevTxIdxNormal, uint16_t CANdevTxIdxInverted, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Initialize a single SRDO object (either producer or consumer decided at runtime). Must be called in the communication reset section. Wires object dictionary communication parameters (0x1301+SRDO_Index) and mapping parameters (0x1381+SRDO_Index), CAN receive/transmit modules and buffers for both normal and inverted messages, and associates emergency reporting and node ID/COB-ID defaults. On parameter structure errors it returns CO_ERROR_OD_PARAMETERS; on values errors the module may emit an emergency (CO_EM_SRDO_CONFIGURATION).
requirements: Call during the communication reset section.
SRDOGuard must have been successfully initialized by CO_SRDOGuard_init().
SRDO must point to writable storage for a CO_SRDO_t instance.
SRDO_Index is the zero-based SRDO index (0 for the first).
OD must be a valid pointer to the CANopen Object Dictionary for the node.
em must be a valid pointer to the Emergency object (CO_EM_t).
nodeId is the local node ID; if default COB-IDs are used, nodeId is added to them per stack rules.
defaultCOB_ID is the base COB-ID for SRDO when using plain data (without node ID embedded).
OD_130x_SRDOCommPar must reference the SRDO communication parameter record at 0x1301 + SRDO_Index.
OD_138x_SRDOMapPar must reference the SRDO mapping parameter record at 0x1381 + SRDO_Index.
CANdevRxNormal and CANdevRxInverted must be valid CAN device modules configured for reception; their indices (CANdevRxIdxNormal, CANdevRxIdxInverted) must be valid for those modules.
CANdevTxNormal and CANdevTxInverted must be valid CAN device modules configured for transmission; their indices (CANdevTxIdxNormal, CANdevTxIdxInverted) must be valid for those modules.
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL it is written with additional error information on failure.
Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid inputs; CO_ERROR_OD_PARAMETERS on invalid OD parameter structure.

functions.name: CO_SRDO_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_SRDO_initCallbackPre(CO_SRDO_t* SRDO, void* object, void (*pFunctSignalPre)(void* object));
functions.description: Install an optional pre-processing callback that should promptly trigger CO_SRDO_process() when an SRDO message is received. Intended to minimize latency between CAN reception and SRDO processing. This API is compiled only when CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE is enabled in CO_CONFIG_SRDO.
requirements: Available only if ((CO_CONFIG_SRDO & CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE) != 0).
SRDO must be a valid, initialized CO_SRDO_t instance.
object is an opaque user pointer passed back to the callback; it may be NULL.
pFunctSignalPre may be NULL to disable the callback; if non-NULL it must be callable at interrupt or high-priority context if used that way by the CAN driver.
The callback should trigger scheduling of CO_SRDO_process() quickly after reception, as message transmission/processing timing is safety-critical.

functions.name: CO_SRDO_config
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_SRDO_config(CO_SRDO_t* SRDO, uint8_t SRDO_Index, CO_SRDOGuard_t* SRDOGuard, uint32_t* errInfo);
functions.description: Configure an SRDO object from its OD parameters and current NMT state. Must be called on transition to NMT operational; it is also invoked from CO_SRDO_init(). Applies OD communication/mapping parameters and readies CAN reception/transmission for normal and inverted frames.
requirements: Call on transition to NMT operational for each SRDO; also called from CO_SRDO_init().
SRDO must point to an SRDO object previously initialized by CO_SRDO_init().
SRDOGuard must be a valid pointer to the guard object used during initialization.
SRDO_Index is the zero-based SRDO index (0 for the first) matching the OD entries used at init.
errInfo may be NULL; if non-NULL it is written with additional error information on failure.
Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success; CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid inputs; CO_ERROR_OD_PARAMETERS on invalid OD parameter values.

functions.name: CO_SRDO_requestSend
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_SRDO_requestSend(CO_SRDO_t* SRDO);
functions.description: Request an SRDO to be sent before the next refresh timer fires; the actual transmission occurs inside CO_SRDO_process(). After the pair of transmissions, the refresh timer is reset to the full cycle time. Intended for event-driven send within the constraints of SRDO timing.
requirements: SRDO must point to a valid, configured CO_SRDO_t instance.
This request must be followed by timely execution of CO_SRDO_process() by the RTOS/main loop to perform the actual send.
Effective primarily when the SRDO is configured as a producer (tx); behavior for consumer SRDOs is implementation-defined/ignored.
Returns CO_ERROR_NO if the request is accepted; other return codes may indicate the request cannot be granted (specific codes not documented here).

functions.name: CO_SRDO_process
functions.signature: CO_SRDO_state_t CO_SRDO_process(CO_SRDO_t* SRDO, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us, bool_t NMTisOperational);
functions.description: Cyclically process a single SRDO object for transmission or reception. Handles timing for normal/inverted frames, validates delays and timeouts, and updates the internal safety communication state. Should be called regularly in the main loop or task. Returns the current internal state, which the application can use to determine whether the device may remain in working state or must go to safe state.
requirements: Call periodically; timeDifference_us must be the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call for this SRDO.
SRDO must be a valid, configured CO_SRDO_t instance.
timerNext_us may be NULL; if non-NULL, the function may write the recommended time until the next call.
NMTisOperational must reflect the current NMT state of the node (true for NMT operational).
The function is designed to be fast and non-blocking; it should be scheduled frequently enough to meet SRDO timing (SCT/SRVT) requirements of the application.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_LSSmaster_init(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint16_t timeout_ms, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, uint16_t CANidLssSlave, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx, uint16_t CANdevTxIdx, uint16_t CANidLssMaster);
functions.description: Initialize the LSS master object and bind it to CAN RX/TX resources and COB-IDs. Must be called during the CANopen communication reset phase. Sets the LSS response timeout and prepares internal state and CAN buffers. Only available when LSS master is enabled at build time.
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section (during CANopenNode initialization/reset).
LSSmaster must be a valid, writable pointer to an allocated CO_LSSmaster_t.
timeout_ms is in milliseconds; it defines the per-transfer LSS response timeout.
CANdevRx and CANdevTx must be valid, initialized CAN modules for LSS reception/transmission, respectively.
CANdevRxIdx and CANdevTxIdx must refer to valid buffer indices within the provided CAN modules.
CANidLssSlave is the COB-ID used for LSS slave-to-master (reception) and must be valid for the CAN controller/network.
CANidLssMaster is the COB-ID used for LSS master-to-slave (transmission) and must be valid for the CAN controller/network.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.
Caller must check the return value (CO_ERROR_NO on success, CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid args).

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_changeTimeout
functions.signature: void CO_LSSmaster_changeTimeout(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint16_t timeout_ms);
functions.description: Change the LSS master per-transfer response timeout. Affects how long the master waits for a slave reply before timing out. Lower values can speed up negative-ack based flows (e.g., fastscan) but increase risk of late responses.
requirements: LSSmaster must be a valid pointer to an initialized CO_LSSmaster_t.
timeout_ms is specified in milliseconds and applies per LSS transfer; multi-transfer commands apply this timeout to each transfer.
Selecting a timeout that is too low may cause late responses and protocol errors; choose as high as necessary and as low as possible.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_LSSmaster_initCallbackPre(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, void* object, void (*pFunctSignal)(void* object));
functions.description: Register an optional pre-receive callback that is invoked immediately after an LSS message is received. Intended to wake/signal an RTOS task to continue LSS processing. Has no effect if callback is NULL.
requirements: Available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE) != 0 at compile time.
LSSmaster must be a valid pointer to an initialized CO_LSSmaster_t.
object may be NULL; if provided, it is passed to the callback.
pFunctSignal may be NULL (disables the callback); if non-NULL it must be callable and return quickly (should only signal/wake tasks).

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_swStateSelect
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_swStateSelect(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint32_t timeDifference_us, CO_LSS_address_t* lssAddress);
functions.description: Select LSS target(s) for subsequent commands. Selects a specific node by LSS address or all nodes when lssAddress is NULL. Non-blocking; call cyclically until it returns a value other than CO_LSSmaster_WAIT_SLAVE.
requirements: LSSmaster must be initialized and not currently processing another LSS request (otherwise returns CO_LSSmaster_INVALID_STATE).
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; pass 0 on the first call to start the request.
lssAddress may be NULL to select all nodes; otherwise must point to a valid CO_LSS_address_t.
Only one selection can be active at any time.
Caller must repeatedly invoke this function until it returns not CO_LSSmaster_WAIT_SLAVE and handle CO_LSSmaster_TIMEOUT or other error returns.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_swStateDeselect
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_swStateDeselect(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster);
functions.description: Deselect all nodes and reset the LSS master state machine to a clean state. Ends any ongoing selection state.
requirements: LSSmaster must be a valid pointer to an initialized CO_LSSmaster_t.
May return CO_LSSmaster_INVALID_STATE if state machine is not ready.
Caller must check the return value for CO_LSSmaster_OK or an error.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_configureBitTiming
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_configureBitTiming(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint16_t bit);
functions.description: Request to set a new bit timing value in the selected node. The new bitrate is staged as a pending value in the slave (not yet active). Non-blocking; call cyclically until completion.
requirements: Exactly one specific node must be selected before calling; calling with no or multiple nodes selected results in CO_LSSmaster_INVALID_STATE.
LSSmaster must not be busy with another LSS request.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; pass 0 on the first call to start the request.
bit is the requested bit timing value; valid encodings/values are device-specific and may be rejected with manufacturer/illegal-argument status.
Caller must loop until return != CO_LSSmaster_WAIT_SLAVE and handle CO_LSSmaster_TIMEOUT, CO_LSSmaster_OK_MANUFACTURER, and CO_LSSmaster_OK_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT appropriately.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_configureNodeId
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_configureNodeId(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint8_t nodeId);
functions.description: Request to set a new node ID in the selected node. The new node ID is staged as a pending value in the slave. Non-blocking; call cyclically until completion.
requirements: Exactly one specific node must be selected before calling; calling with no or multiple nodes selected results in CO_LSSmaster_INVALID_STATE.
LSSmaster must not be busy with another LSS request.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; pass 0 on the first call to start the request.
nodeId is the requested node ID; the special value CO_LSS_NODE_ID_ASSIGNMENT can be used to invalidate the node ID; other range rules are not specified here and may be rejected by the node.
Caller must loop until return != CO_LSSmaster_WAIT_SLAVE and handle CO_LSSmaster_TIMEOUT, CO_LSSmaster_OK_MANUFACTURER, and CO_LSSmaster_OK_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT appropriately.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_configureStore
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_configureStore(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint32_t timeDifference_us);
functions.description: Request the selected node to store its current pending bit timing and node ID as permanent values. Non-blocking; call cyclically until completion.
requirements: Exactly one specific node must be selected before calling; calling with no or multiple nodes selected results in CO_LSSmaster_INVALID_STATE.
LSSmaster must not be busy with another LSS request.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; pass 0 on the first call to start the request.
Caller must loop until return != CO_LSSmaster_WAIT_SLAVE and handle CO_LSSmaster_TIMEOUT and manufacturer/illegal-argument results as returned.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_ActivateBit
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_ActivateBit(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint16_t switchDelay_ms);
functions.description: Request activation of the pending bit timing in slaves. Critical network operation intended to switch all nodes to the new bitrate nearly simultaneously. Requires all nodes to be selected.
requirements: All nodes that must switch must be selected when calling this function (select all nodes).
Only call after all nodes have accepted the new bit timing as pending and support changing bit timing, otherwise network may become unusable.
LSSmaster must be a valid pointer to an initialized CO_LSSmaster_t and not busy with another LSS request.
switchDelay_ms specifies the slave-applied delay before and after switching, in milliseconds.
Caller must check the return value for CO_LSSmaster_OK or an error (CO_LSSmaster_INVALID_STATE / CO_LSSmaster_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT).
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_InquireLssAddress
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_InquireLssAddress(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint32_t timeDifference_us, CO_LSS_address_t* lssAddress);
functions.description: Read the LSS address (vendor ID, product code, revision, serial) from the currently selected node. Useful after selecting a node by fastscan. Non-blocking; call cyclically until completion.
requirements: Exactly one specific node must be selected before calling.
LSSmaster must not be busy with another LSS request.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; pass 0 on the first call to start the request.
lssAddress must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the result on success.
Caller must loop until return != CO_LSSmaster_WAIT_SLAVE and handle CO_LSSmaster_TIMEOUT or other error returns.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_Inquire
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_Inquire(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint8_t lssInquireCs, uint32_t* value);
functions.description: Read either the node ID or one part of the LSS address (vendor ID, product code, revision, serial) from the selected node. The specific field is chosen by lssInquireCs. Non-blocking; call cyclically until completion.
requirements: Exactly one specific node must be selected before calling.
LSSmaster must not be busy with another LSS request.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; pass 0 on the first call to start the request.
lssInquireCs must be one of the CO_LSS_INQUIRE_xx command specifiers defined in CO_LSS_command_specifiers.
value must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the 32-bit result on success.
Caller must loop until return != CO_LSSmaster_WAIT_SLAVE and handle CO_LSSmaster_TIMEOUT or other error returns.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSmaster_IdentifyFastscan
functions.signature: CO_LSSmaster_return_t CO_LSSmaster_IdentifyFastscan(CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster, uint32_t timeDifference_us, CO_LSSmaster_fastscan_t* fastscan);
functions.description: Perform LSS identify fastscan to select an unconfigured node matching given criteria. Supports full scan, partial scan, or verification per address part. On completion, either a node is selected, or none if criteria do not match or all nodes are configured. Non-blocking; call cyclically until it completes.
requirements: No node may be selected when starting the scan process.
Provide a valid fastscan structure; for each of the 4 address parts, set fastscan.scan[...] to SCAN/SKIP/MATCH and, for MATCH, provide the comparison value in fastscan.match.
fastscan.found will be populated with the discovered address when a node is found.
Scanning limitations: no more than two values can be skipped; the Vendor ID cannot be skipped.
When doing partial scans, the user must ensure the resulting LSS address criteria uniquely identify a single node.
LSSmaster must not be busy with another LSS request.
timeDifference_us is the elapsed time in microseconds since the previous call; pass 0 on the first call to start the request.
Caller must loop until return != CO_LSSmaster_WAIT_SLAVE and handle returns: CO_LSSmaster_SCAN_FINISHED, CO_LSSmaster_SCAN_NOACK, CO_LSSmaster_SCAN_FAILED.
Function is available only if (CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_LSS_MASTER) != 0 at compile time.

functions.name: CO_LSSslave_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_LSSslave_init(CO_LSSslave_t* LSSslave, CO_LSS_address_t* lssAddress, uint16_t* pendingBitRate, uint8_t* pendingNodeID, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevRx, uint16_t CANdevRxIdx, uint16_t CANidLssMaster, CO_CANmodule_t* CANdevTx, uint16_t CANdevTxIdx, uint16_t CANidLssSlave)
functions.description: Initialize an LSS (Layer Setting Services) slave object and bind it to CAN RX/TX resources. Intended to be called during the communication-reset phase of node startup (between CO_CANinit and CO_CANopenInit). It wires in pointers to persistent, application-owned variables for pending CAN bit-rate and node ID that LSS may update, and prepares CAN filters/buffers for LSS traffic. If the pending node ID is valid (1..0x7F), it becomes the active node ID immediately; if it is 0xFF (unconfigured), only the LSS slave is started so a master can configure it. Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success or CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT for bad inputs. Note: The LSS address must be unique and derived from a fully initialized Identity Object (1018h).
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section, between CO_CANinit() and CO_CANopenInit().
Argument LSSslave must be a valid pointer to storage that will hold the initialized object.
Argument lssAddress must point to a fully initialized, unique LSS address (Identity Object 1018h fields vendorID, product code, revisionNo, serialNo must be valid).
Arguments pendingBitRate and pendingNodeID must point to external (application-owned) variables initialized at startup (after CO_NMT_RESET_NODE) from NVM, DIP switches, etc.
pendingBitRate and pendingNodeID must not change during CO_NMT_RESET_COMMUNICATION; they may be modified by CO_LSSslave_process() based on master commands.

If *pendingNodeID is 1..0x7F at function exit, that value becomes the active node ID and other CANopen objects may be initialized; if *pendingNodeID is 0xFF, only the LSS slave runs until configuration completes.

CANdevRx and CANdevTx must be valid CAN device handles; CANdevRxIdx and CANdevTxIdx must be valid buffer indices for those devices; CANidLssMaster and CANidLssSlave must be valid COB-IDs for LSS communication.
Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success or CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid arguments.

functions.name: CO_LSSslave_process
functions.signature: bool_t CO_LSSslave_process(CO_LSSslave_t* LSSslave)
functions.description: Mainline processing for the LSS slave. Completes handling of LSS services that were pre-processed on CAN reception and may request a CANopen communication reset when a valid node ID is configured by the LSS master. Returns true when a CO_NMT_RESET_COMMUNICATION is requested.
requirements: Argument LSSslave must point to an LSS slave previously initialized with CO_LSSslave_init().
Should be called from the application’s main processing loop whenever LSS is enabled/active.
Caller must act on a true return value by performing a communication reset as appropriate for the application.

functions.name: CO_LSSslave_getState
functions.signature: static inline uint8_t CO_LSSslave_getState(CO_LSSslave_t* LSSslave)
functions.description: Lightweight accessor for the current LSS slave state. Returns the internal state code, or CO_LSS_STATE_WAITING if LSSslave is NULL. Intended for quick checks of the LSS state from application code.
requirements: LSSslave may be NULL; in that case the function returns CO_LSS_STATE_WAITING.
If non-NULL, LSSslave should be an initialized LSS slave object.

functions.name: CO_LSSslave_initCallbackPre
functions.signature: void CO_LSSslave_initCallbackPre(CO_LSSslave_t* LSSslave, void* object, void (*pFunctSignalPre)(void* object))
functions.description: Register an optional pre-processing callback invoked immediately after an LSS message is received, allowing the application/RTOS to promptly schedule further LSS processing (e.g., wake a task). If pFunctSignalPre is NULL, no callback is invoked. Available only when CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE is enabled at compile time.
requirements: This function is compiled/available only if ((CO_CONFIG_LSS & CO_CONFIG_FLAG_CALLBACK_PRE) != 0) or CO_DOXYGEN is defined.
Argument LSSslave must be a valid LSS slave object (typically initialized via CO_LSSslave_init()).
Argument object is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; it may be NULL.
Argument pFunctSignalPre may be NULL; if NULL, no callback will be called.

functions.name: CO_LSSslave_initCkBitRateCall
functions.signature: void CO_LSSslave_initCkBitRateCall(CO_LSSslave_t* LSSslave, void* object, bool_t (*pFunctLSScheckBitRate)(void* object, uint16_t bitRate))
functions.description: Register a callback used to verify support for a requested CAN bit rate when the LSS master sends a “configure bit timing parameters” command. The callback should return true if the bit rate is supported; if no callback is set, the slave will not acknowledge the request, indicating that changing bit rate is not supported.
requirements: Argument LSSslave must be a valid LSS slave object.
Argument object is passed through to the callback and may be NULL.
Argument pFunctLSScheckBitRate may be NULL; if NULL, the LSS slave will no-ack bit rate change requests.
The callback must accept the requested bitRate (in kbps as per stack conventions) and return true if supported; false otherwise.

functions.name: CO_LSSslave_initActBitRateCall
functions.signature: void CO_LSSslave_initActBitRateCall(CO_LSSslave_t* LSSslave, void* object, void (*pFunctLSSactivateBitRate)(void* object, uint16_t delay))
functions.description: Register a callback invoked when the LSS master issues “activate bit timing parameters”. The callback allows the application to apply the specified delay (milliseconds) before and after switching bit rates as per CiA DSP 305 section 6.4.4. During the delay periods the device must not transmit any CAN frames. If the callback is NULL, it will not be called.
requirements: Argument LSSslave must be a valid LSS slave object.
Argument object is passed to the callback and may be NULL.
Argument pFunctLSSactivateBitRate may be NULL; if NULL, no activation callback is performed.
Callback receives the delay parameter in milliseconds and must ensure the device refrains from sending messages during the specified pre- and post-switch delays, per DSP 305 6.4.4.

functions.name: CO_LSSslave_initCfgStoreCall
functions.signature: void CO_LSSslave_initCfgStoreCall(CO_LSSslave_t* LSSslave, void* object, bool_t (*pFunctLSScfgStore)(void* object, uint8_t id, uint16_t bitRate))
functions.description: Register a callback to persist LSS configuration (“store configuration”). The callback should store the provided node ID and bit rate to non-volatile memory so they can be supplied as persistent values after reset. If the callback returns true, the LSS slave reports success to the master; if no callback is set, the LSS slave will not acknowledge the store request (i.e., storing not supported).
requirements: Argument LSSslave must be a valid LSS slave object.
Argument object is passed to the callback and may be NULL.
Argument pFunctLSScfgStore may be NULL; if NULL, the LSS slave will no-ack store configuration requests.
The callback must return true only if the node ID and bitRate were stored successfully in NVM such that they can be re-supplied to CO_LSSslave_init() after reset.

functions.name: CO_GTWA_init
functions.signature:
CO_ReturnError_t CO_GTWA_init(CO_GTWA_t* gtwa,
#if (((CO_CONFIG_GTW)&CO_CONFIG_GTW_ASCII_SDO) != 0) || defined CO_DOXYGEN
                              CO_SDOclient_t* SDO_C, uint16_t SDOclientTimeoutTime_ms, bool_t SDOclientBlockTransfer,
#endif
#if (((CO_CONFIG_GTW)&CO_CONFIG_GTW_ASCII_NMT) != 0) || defined CO_DOXYGEN
                              CO_NMT_t* NMT,
#endif
#if (((CO_CONFIG_GTW)&CO_CONFIG_GTW_ASCII_LSS) != 0) || defined CO_DOXYGEN
                              CO_LSSmaster_t* LSSmaster,
#endif
#if (((CO_CONFIG_GTW)&CO_CONFIG_GTW_ASCII_PRINT_LEDS) != 0) || defined CO_DOXYGEN
                              CO_LEDs_t* LEDs,
#endif
                              uint8_t dummy);
functions.description: Initialize a Gateway-ASCII (CiA 309-3) interface object. It wires optional subsystem objects (SDO client, NMT, LSS master, LEDs) depending on build-time configuration, and sets default SDO timeouts and block-transfer mode when applicable. Use this before any other CO_GTWA_* API and then drive the object with CO_GTWA_process(). Returns CO_ERROR_NO on success or CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid inputs.
requirements: gtwa must be a valid, writable pointer to a CO_GTWA_t instance.
dummy must be set to 0.
If ASCII_SDO is enabled, SDO_C must point to a valid CO_SDOclient_t and SDOclientTimeoutTime_ms is in milliseconds; SDOclientBlockTransfer selects default SDO block mode.
If ASCII_NMT is enabled, NMT must point to a valid CO_NMT_t.
If ASCII_LSS is enabled, LSSmaster must point to a valid CO_LSSmaster_t.
If ASCII_PRINT_LEDS is enabled, LEDs must point to a valid CO_LEDs_t.
Callers should check the return value and handle CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT.

functions.name: CO_GTWA_initRead
functions.description: Register the output callback used by the gateway to deliver response bytes to the application. CO_GTWA_process() invokes this callback zero or more times depending on available data. If the callback is NULL or not registered, output data is purged.
requirements: gtwa must be a valid pointer to an initialized CO_GTWA_t.
readCallback may be NULL; when NULL, outgoing data will be discarded.
If provided, readCallback must safely handle being called from CO_GTWA_process(), and must return the number of bytes actually transferred and may set connectionOK (nonzero indicates connection OK).
readCallbackObject is an opaque pointer passed back as the first parameter to readCallback.

functions.name: CO_GTWA_write_getSpace
functions.signature: static inline size_t CO_GTWA_write_getSpace(CO_GTWA_t* gtwa);
functions.description: Query the remaining free space in the command FIFO into which ASCII commands are written.
requirements: gtwa must be a valid pointer to a CO_GTWA_t.
Use the returned value to avoid overfilling the command buffer before calling CO_GTWA_write().

functions.name: CO_GTWA_write
functions.signature: static inline size_t CO_GTWA_write(CO_GTWA_t* gtwa, const char* buf, size_t count);
functions.description: Append bytes of an ASCII command into the gateway’s internal command FIFO. Commands must be terminated by a '\n'. Partial writes are allowed; if the FIFO lacks space, fewer bytes are copied and the remainder can be written later.
requirements: gtwa must be a valid pointer to a CO_GTWA_t.
buf must point to at least count bytes if count > 0.
Each complete command must be terminated with a '\n' character; '\r' is optional before '\n'.
This function does not null-terminate input; callers must supply the newline.
Caller should handle partial writes by retrying when more space is available (see CO_GTWA_write_getSpace()).

functions.name: CO_GTWA_log_print
functions.signature: void CO_GTWA_log_print(CO_GTWA_t* gtwa, const char* message);
functions.description: Record a message into the gateway’s circular log FIFO for later retrieval via the non-standard "log" command. If the FIFO is full, old messages are overwritten. A newline '\n' is automatically inserted between messages.
requirements: Available only when (CO_CONFIG_GTW & CO_CONFIG_GTW_ASCII_LOG) != 0 or CO_DOXYGEN is defined at build time.
gtwa must be a valid pointer to a CO_GTWA_t.
message must be a null-terminated string.
message must not contain "\r\n" inside.

functions.name: CO_GTWA_process
functions.signature: void CO_GTWA_process(CO_GTWA_t* gtwa, bool_t enable, uint32_t timeDifference_us, uint32_t* timerNext_us);
functions.description: Run the non-blocking Gateway-ASCII state machine. Call cyclically to parse commands, execute SDO/NMT/LSS operations, and emit responses via the registered read callback. When disabled, the gateway ignores command interaction.
requirements: gtwa must be a valid pointer to an initialized CO_GTWA_t.
This function must be called periodically; timeDifference_us is the elapsed time since the previous call, in microseconds.
timerNext_us must be a valid pointer for receiving the suggested next call time (per CO_process conventions).
If enable is false, the gateway is disabled and no command interaction occurs.

functions.name: CO_storage_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_storage_init(CO_storage_t* storage, CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule, OD_entry_t* OD_1010_StoreParameters, OD_entry_t* OD_1011_RestoreDefaultParameters, ODR_t (*store)(CO_storage_entry_t* entry, CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule), ODR_t (*restore)(CO_storage_entry_t* entry, CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule), CO_storage_entry_t* entries, uint8_t entriesCount)
functions.description: Initializes the CANopen data storage base object and installs OD extensions for indices 0x1010 (Store parameters) and 0x1011 (Restore default parameters). Intended to be called by the application after startup and before CO_CANopenInit(). This does not load any stored data; loading is target-specific. The provided store/restore callbacks will be invoked when the respective OD entries are written, with entry->subIndexOD matching the accessed sub-index, and should return an ODR_t status (ODR_OK on success, ODR_HW on hardware error). The entries array lists storage entries and must be application-provided and persistent.
requirements: Call after program startup and before CO_CANopenInit().
storage must point to a valid CO_storage_t that persists for the program lifetime.
OD_1010_StoreParameters may be NULL (optional OD entry).
OD_1011_RestoreDefaultParameters may be NULL (optional OD entry).
store must be a valid function pointer of type ODR_t (*)(CO_storage_entry_t*, CO_CANmodule_t*); it will be called on OD 0x1010 writes and must return ODR_OK on success or ODR_HW on hardware error.
restore must be a valid function pointer of type ODR_t (*)(CO_storage_entry_t*, CO_CANmodule_t*); it will be called on OD 0x1011 writes and must return ODR_OK on success or ODR_HW on hardware error.
entries must point to an application-defined array of CO_storage_entry_t that is initialized and exists permanently.
entriesCount must be the number of elements in entries (fits in uint8_t).
Caller should check the return value: CO_ERROR_NO on success or CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT on invalid arguments.

functions.name: CO_storageEeprom_init
functions.signature: CO_ReturnError_t CO_storageEeprom_init(CO_storage_t* storage, CO_CANmodule_t* CANmodule, void* storageModule, OD_entry_t* OD_1010_StoreParameters, OD_entry_t* OD_1011_RestoreDefaultParam, CO_storage_entry_t* entries, uint8_t entriesCount, uint32_t* storageInitError)
functions.description: Initializes the EEPROM-backed CANopen storage object and OD extensions (0x1010/0x1011), reads/verifies existing data/signatures from EEPROM, and writes validated data to their target addresses. Intended to be called once after program startup and before CO_CANopenInit(). On return, storageInitError provides details if data were corrupt or hardware is missing. Uses the target’s CO_eeprom implementation via storageModule. Internally calls CO_storage_init().
requirements: Must be called after program startup and before CO_CANopenInit().
Parameter storage must point to a valid CO_storage_t object that persists for the program lifetime.
Parameter storageModule must be a valid handle/context expected by the platform’s CO_eeprom implementation.
Parameter CANmodule is for optional usage; may be NULL if unused by target.
Parameters OD_1010_StoreParameters and OD_1011_RestoreDefaultParam are optional; may be NULL.
Parameter entries must point to a valid array of initialized CO_storage_entry_t entries as required by CO_storage_init.
entriesCount must be <= CO_CONFIG_STORAGE_MAX_ENTRIES_COUNT.
Parameter storageInitError must be a valid non-NULL pointer to receive error details.
Caller should check the return value: CO_ERROR_NO on success; CO_ERROR_DATA_CORRUPT, CO_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ARGUMENT, or CO_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY on failure.

If return is CO_ERROR_DATA_CORRUPT and storageInitError equals 0xFFFFFFFF, it indicates a hardware error (e.g., missing EEPROM); otherwise storageInitError is a bitmask of subIndexODs or an entry index as documented.

functions.name: CO_storageEeprom_auto_process
functions.signature: void CO_storageEeprom_auto_process(CO_storage_t* storage, bool_t saveAll)
functions.description: Periodically updates EEPROM-stored data for entries marked with auto storage, writing one byte per call. When saveAll is true, writes all pending bytes (useful during shutdown). For auto storage to operate, the corresponding entry’s EEPROM signature must be valid; CRC is not used for auto updates.
requirements: Must be called cyclically by the application for incremental background saving; call with saveAll=true to flush all bytes (e.g., at program end).
Parameter storage must point to a previously initialized CO_storage_t (e.g., via CO_storageEeprom_init/CO_storage_init) that remains valid.
Only entries configured with CO_storage_auto are updated.
Auto storage requires that the entry’s EEPROM signature is valid; otherwise auto updates for that entry will not occur.

functions.name: CO_eeprom_init
functions.signature: bool_t CO_eeprom_init(void* storageModule)
functions.description: Initialize the EEPROM device for use with CO_storageEeprom on the target system. Call this once before any other EEPROM access routines. Returns true on successful initialization.
requirements: storageModule must be a valid pointer to a storage module object expected by the target implementation (opaque here).
Must be called before CO_eeprom_getAddr, CO_eeprom_readBlock, CO_eeprom_writeBlock, CO_eeprom_getCrcBlock, and CO_eeprom_updateByte.
Caller must check the boolean return value to confirm successful initialization.

functions.name: CO_eeprom_getAddr
functions.signature: size_t CO_eeprom_getAddr(void* storageModule, bool_t isAuto, size_t len, bool_t* overflow)
functions.description: Obtain a free EEPROM address range to store a block of data. Intended to be called several times during the initialization phase after CO_eeprom_init(), once per storage block. Sets overflow to true if there is not enough EEPROM space.
requirements: Must be called after a successful CO_eeprom_init call.
storageModule must be a valid pointer to the storage module object.
overflow must be a non-null pointer to receive the overflow flag.
len specifies the length of data to be stored at the assigned location; the returned address must be used consistently with this length.
isAuto indicates whether the variable is automatically stored (true) or protected (false).
Caller must handle the case where *overflow is set to true (indicating insufficient EEPROM memory).
Returned address must be considered valid only within the target EEPROM address space; behavior for invalid lengths or out-of-range requests is unspecified by this header.

functions.name: CO_eeprom_readBlock
functions.signature: void CO_eeprom_readBlock(void* storageModule, uint8_t* data, size_t eepromAddr, size_t len)
functions.description: Read a contiguous block of bytes from EEPROM into the provided buffer. Intended for target-specific EEPROM backends.
requirements: Must be called after a successful CO_eeprom_init call.
storageModule must be a valid pointer to the storage module object.
data must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
eepromAddr and len must designate a valid readable range within the EEPROM device; out-of-range behavior is undefined by this header.
Caller must ensure any device-specific alignment or timing constraints required by the target implementation are met (not specified here).

functions.name: CO_eeprom_writeBlock
functions.signature: bool_t CO_eeprom_writeBlock(void* storageModule, uint8_t* data, size_t eepromAddr, size_t len)
functions.description: Write a contiguous block of bytes to EEPROM from the provided buffer. This function is blocking and returns only after the write completes. If data spans multiple pages, eepromAddr must be page-aligned per the target’s EEPROM page size. Returns true on success.
requirements: Must be called after a successful CO_eeprom_init call.
storageModule must be a valid pointer to the storage module object.
data must point to a readable buffer of at least len bytes.
eepromAddr and len must designate a valid writable range within the EEPROM device.
If the data crosses multiple EEPROM pages, eepromAddr must be aligned to the EEPROM page boundary as required by the target implementation.
Caller must check the boolean return value to detect write failures.
This function blocks until completion; callers should avoid calling from time-critical contexts if blocking is unacceptable.

functions.name: CO_eeprom_getCrcBlock
functions.signature: uint16_t CO_eeprom_getCrcBlock(void* storageModule, size_t eepromAddr, size_t len)
functions.description: Compute and return the CRC checksum of a block of data stored in EEPROM at the given address and length. The specific CRC algorithm/parameters are not detailed in this header (unknown; target-specific).
requirements: Must be called after a successful CO_eeprom_init call.
storageModule must be a valid pointer to the storage module object.
eepromAddr and len must designate a valid readable range within the EEPROM device.
Caller should assume the CRC algorithm is target-specific; interoperability requires using the same backend routine for both writing/verifying.

functions.name: CO_eeprom_updateByte
functions.signature: bool_t CO_eeprom_updateByte(void* storageModule, uint8_t data, size_t eepromAddr)
functions.description: Update a single byte in EEPROM, writing only if the current stored value differs. Used by automatic storage. Returns true if the write completed successfully, or false if the device is still busy finishing a previous write.
requirements: Must be called after a successful CO_eeprom_init call.
storageModule must be a valid pointer to the storage module object.
eepromAddr must be a valid writable address within the EEPROM device.
Caller must be prepared to handle a false return (device busy) and retry or defer until the previous write completes.
Intended for automatic storage use-cases; frequent calls may be serialized by EEPROM write-cycle timing constraints.

functions.name: CO_trace_init
functions.signature: void CO_trace_init(CO_trace_t *trace, CO_SDO_t *SDO, uint8_t enabled, uint32_t *timeBuffer, int32_t *valueBuffer, uint32_t bufferSize, uint32_t *map, uint8_t *format, uint8_t *trigger, int32_t *threshold, int32_t *value, int32_t *minValue, int32_t *maxValue, uint32_t *triggerTime, uint16_t idx_OD_traceConfig, uint16_t idx_OD_trace)
functions.description: Initialize a CANopen trace object that samples a mapped Object Dictionary variable and stores timestamped values in circular buffers. Intended to be invoked during the CANopen communication reset section. The trace configuration (mapping, format, trigger behavior, statistics and exposure via SDO) is bound to Object Dictionary entries passed in. After initialization, periodic sampling is performed by CO_trace_process().
requirements: Must be called in the communication reset section (explicit).
trace must point to a valid CO_trace_t to be initialized (inferred from parameter description).
SDO must point to a valid SDO server object associated with the node (inferred from parameter description).
timeBuffer must point to a memory block for storing time records with at least bufferSize elements of uint32_t (explicit).
valueBuffer must point to a memory block for storing value records with at least bufferSize elements of int32_t (explicit).
bufferSize specifies the capacity of both timeBuffer and valueBuffer in elements; both buffers must match this size (explicit).
map must reference a valid PDO-style mapping to the OD variable to be monitored (explicit).
format must reference a valid format specifier as defined by the Object Dictionary; if the first bit is 1, the monitored variable is treated as unsigned (explicit).
trigger controls trigger recording; if the value is nonzero, trigger time is recorded when the variable crosses threshold (explicit; pointer must reference valid storage).
threshold must point to the threshold value used with trigger (explicit; pointer must reference valid storage).
value must point to writable storage that will hold the last sampled value (explicit).
minValue must point to writable storage that will hold the minimum observed value (explicit).
maxValue must point to writable storage that will hold the maximum observed value (explicit).
triggerTime must point to writable storage that will hold the last trigger time (explicit).
idx_OD_traceConfig must be the index of the trace configuration entry in the Object Dictionary (explicit).
idx_OD_trace must be the index of the trace data/plot entry in the Object Dictionary (explicit).
CO_trace_process() must be used after initialization to perform sampling (inferred from overall design).

functions.name: CO_trace_process
functions.signature: void CO_trace_process(CO_trace_t *trace, uint32_t timestamp)
functions.description: Periodically process a trace object: sample the mapped OD variable and, when it changes, store a timestamped record into the circular buffer. Also updates statistics and trigger timing per the configuration. Designed to be called at 1 ms intervals; data can later be retrieved via SDO as an SVG plot generated by the trace object.
requirements: Must be called cyclically in 1 ms intervals (explicit).
trace must be a valid, previously initialized CO_trace_t via CO_trace_init (inferred from usage).
timestamp supplies the current time, usually in millisecond resolution (explicit).
The trace must be enabled via its configuration to record data; otherwise it performs no recording (inferred from struct member and description).
